A Conservative hybrid fund cannot invest more than 25% of their total assets in equity instruments C. A Conservative hybrid fund cannot invest in debt securities which have lower than AAA rating
options: Only A and B are correct
Only A and C are correct
All A, B and C are correct
explanation: Conservative Hybrid Fund is an open-ended hybrid scheme investing predominantly in debt instruments. Investment in debt instruments shall be between 75 percent and 90 percent of total assets while investment in equity and equity instruments shall be between 10 percent and 25 percent of total assets. The word "conservative" in the name of Conservative hybrid funds category only refers to the equity allocation. Therefore, a Conservative hybrid fund cannot invest more than 25% of their total assets in equity instruments. Statement A is incorrect as there is no specific restriction on the Macaulay Duration for the debt portion of a Conservative Hybrid Fund Statement C is incorrect - While these funds are "conservative," they are not prohibited from investing in debt securities rated below AAA.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: If a mutual fund enters into a transaction for purchase or sale of securities with any of its associates, then the members of Asset Management Company of the mutual fund have to ________ .
options: Inform the mutual fund unitholders of the intent to undertake the transaction before it is done
Justify the fairness of the transaction to the Board of Trustees
Make certain that the transactions happens at a price that is better than the closing market price
Take the approval of the trustees before undertaking the transactions
explanation: As per the AMFI Code of Ethics for Mutual Funds : Members shall in respect of transactions of purchase and sale of securities entered into with any of their associates or any significant unitholder : 1. Submit to the Board of Trustees details of such transactions, justifying its fairness to the scheme 2. Disclose to the unitholders details of the transaction in brief through annual and half yearly reports

subject: mutual_funds
stem: In which of the following case can a mutual fund charge the additional expense of 0.30 % of daily net assets of the scheme ?
options: When the new inflows from beyond top 30 cities is at least i) 30% of the gross new inflows in the scheme OR ii) 15% of the average AUM (Year To Date) of the scheme, which ever is higher
When the new inflows from beyond top 25 cities is at least 30% of the gross new inflows
When the new inflows from beyond top 30 cities is at least 10% of the gross new inflows
When the new inflows from beyond top 15 cities is at least 20% of the gross new inflows
explanation: In addition to the regular limits, the following expenses may be charged to the scheme: i. Brokerage and transaction cost which are incurred for the purpose of execution of trade up to 0.12 percent of trade value in case of cash market transactions and 0.05 percent of trade value in case of derivatives transactions. ii. If the new inflows from beyond top 30 cities are at least a) 30 percent of gross new inflows in the scheme or b) 15 percent of the average assets under management (year to date) of the scheme, whichever is higher, funds can charge the additional expense of up to 0.30 percent of the daily net assets of the scheme.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What happens in the process of Indexation?
options: In indexation, the impact of capital gains tax is reduced in case of both short term and long term capital gains
In indexation, the mutual fund's performance is benchmarked against a suitable index
In indexation, the cost of acquisition is adjusted upwards to reflect the impact of inflation
explanation: Indexation means that the cost of acquisition or the cost of purchase is adjusted upwards to reflect the impact of inflation. For eg. - A stock was purchased at Rs 500 and sold for Rs 800 after 5 years. The long term capital gains is Rs 300 on which tax is to paid. But when adjusted for indexation, the capital gains will be reduced and the tax will have to be paid on a lower amount.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: In case one of the joint holders dies, then the units will ________ .
options: be transferred to the HUF of deceased holder
continue to be held by surviving joint holders
explanation: Once a mutual fund folio is created as a jointly held account there can be no change in the joint holders. A joint holder cannot be deleted or a new one added, except in the event of death. In the event of a death of a joint holder. his/her name is deleted and the surviving joint holders can continue with the investment.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: _______ is not included in the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme.
options: Liquidity provisions such as listing, repurchase, redemption
Aggregate fees and expenses charged to the scheme
Any safety net or guarantee provided
explanation: As per SEBI regulations, the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme include: Type of scheme Investment objectives Liquidity provisions (repurchase/redemption/listing) Aggregate fees and expenses Any safety net or guarantee Exit load is NOT a fundamental attribute.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these statements is true with respect to Key Information Memorandum (KIM)?
options: KIM is a document that provides key information of the past performance of the scheme
KIM is the annual newsletter of the mutual fund
KIM provided NAV history of all mutual fund schemes
KIM is a document which must accompany all mutual fund application forms
explanation: While an investor is expected to read all the scheme related documents, circulation of the same along with the application forms is too difficult and costly, especially if the printed forms are to be distributed. In order to ensure the investor gets access to sufficient information in spite of such a constraint, a Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is mandatorily circulated along with the application form.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Dividing an individual's portfolio allocation between Core portfolio and Satellite portfolio is dependent on the risk profile of the investor - State whether True or False?
explanation: Ideally an investor's portfolio should be divided into Core and Satellite portfolios. The core portfolio will be invested according to the long-term needs of the investor and the satellite portfolio will be invested to take advantage of expected short-term market movements. However, the division between core and satellite portfolios will depend upon each investor's profile. Conservative investors may like a very small proportion of their overall portfolio to be managed tactically and an investor comfortable with taking higher risk may have an even higher exposure to tactical investments.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Condensed financial information for schemes launched in last 3 financial years is mentioned in the ______________.
explanation: Section I of the SAI gives complete details of the constituents of the mutual fund--Sponsors, AMC and Trustee Company, of service providers {Custodian, Registrar & Transfer Agent, Statutory Auditor, Fund Accountant (if outsourced) and Collecting Bankers}. This includes their experience, condensed financial information (for schemes launched in last 3 financial years), key personnel, rights and obligations and other information the investor may require to evaluate the investment.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: If a investor has to change his default bank account in a mutual fund folio, he/she has to do it with ____ .
explanation: Mutual funds provide investors the facility to register multiple bank accounts to facilitate receiving the redemption, dividends and any other payouts from the fund. An individual investor can register up to five bank accounts. One of the accounts is designated as the default account, and unless otherwise specified all credits are made to this account by the mutual fund. Investors can change the default bank account at any time by instructing the AMC to do so.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement/s. 1. The market liquidity can get impacted due to market related events and company factors 2. There cannot be a price impact on mutual fund units due to liquidity demands due to redemption or portfolio rebalancing
explanation: Statement 1 is true as liquidity can reduce because of market panic/crashes, economic events, bad news about a company etc. Statement 2 is false as large redemptions or portfolio rebalancing may force a mutual fund to sell securities quickly. This can affect security prices and indirectly impact NAV/unit prices.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Tactical Asset Allocation decisions are based on which of these factor/s?
explanation: Tactical asset allocation means changing the investment mix temporarily to benefit from expected market movements. These decisions are mainly based on the expected behavior or trend of the market. For example, if equity markets are expected to rise, more money may be allocated to equities. The purpose of such an approach is to take advantage of the opportunities presented by various markets at different points of time.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these investors CANNOT do CASH investments in mutual funds up to a limit of Rs. 50,000?
options: Investments made by a PIO (Person of Indian Origin)
Investments made by Sole Proprietorship firm
Investments made by resident Indian investors without PAN
explanation: Mutual funds usually do not accept cash. Small investors, who may not be taxpayers and may not have PAN/bank accounts, such as farmers, small traders/businessmen/workers are allowed cash transactions for the purchase of units in mutual funds to the extent of Rs. 50,000/-per investor, per mutual fund, per financial year. This facility is available only for resident individuals, sole proprietorships and minors investing through their guardians. PIO is not among the eligible investors.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Who specifies the heads of expenses that can be charged to a mutual fund scheme by the Asset Management Company?
explanation: Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, Mutual Funds are permitted to charge certain operating expenses for managing a mutual fund scheme - such as sales & marketing / advertising expenses, administrative expenses, transaction costs, investment management fees, registrar fees, custodian fees, audit fees - as a percentage of the fund's daily net assets. All such costs for running and managing a mutual fund scheme are collectively referred to as 'Total Expense Ratio' (TER) The regulatory limits of TER that can be incurred/charged to the fund by a Mutual Fund AMC have been specified under Regulation 52 of SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these statement/s is/are INCORRECT? A. The impact of exit load can be ignored by the distributor at the time of re-purchase of a mutual fund units B. When the investor wants to redeem mutual fund units, the distributor must suggest redemption from the scheme with the maximum exit load
options: Both statements A and B are incorrect
explanation: Both statements describe unethical and incorrect practices that a MF distributor must never follow. Let us understand why each is false: Statement A is FALSE - At the time of repurchase, the MF distributor must inform the investor about the exit load and its impact on the redemption amount. Ignoring exit load means the investor is not getting complete and transparent information - which is a violation of the distributor's duty of proper disclosure. Statement B is FALSE - A distributor must never ask an investor to redeem from a scheme with the maximum exit load. This would cause unnecessary financial loss to the investor. A responsible distributor should instead guide the investor to redeem from a scheme where exit load is nil or minimum, protecting the investor's interest.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following serves as the basis for creating a mutual fund's investment portfolio?
options: Investment objectives defined for the fund
The characteristics of the unit holders
explanation: Every mutual fund scheme is launched with a specific investment objective (e.g., growth, income, balanced, sector-focused). The fund manager designs the portfolio - choosing stocks, bonds, or other securities - to match this objective. The risk appetite, preferences or characteristics of individual investors are not considered while constructing the portfolio, because a mutual fund is a pooled vehicle - hundreds or thousands of investors with different profiles invest together in the same scheme.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the category of investors that does not need to provide a PAN card at the time of investing in mutual funds.
options: Investors whose total annual investment, including SIPs, does not exceed Rs 75,000 per mutual fund
Investors whose annual investment excluding SIPs is capped at Rs 75,000 per mutual fund
Investors whose total annual investment, including SIPs, does not exceed Rs 50,000 per mutual fund
Investors whose annual investment excluding SIPs is capped at Rs 50,000 per mutual fund
explanation: As per SEBI regulations, small investors who invest up to Rs. 50,000 per year per mutual fund are exempted from submitting a PAN card. This is called the "Micro SIP" or small investment exemption - designed to encourage first-time or low-income investors to participate in mutual funds without the barrier of having a PAN card. This limit of Rs. 50,000 includes SIP investments as well - meaning even if you invest through monthly SIPs, the total across the year must stay within Rs. 50,000 to enjoy this exemption.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the true statement(s) from the options given below: A) Indian investors have no option for diversifying in international investments B) One of the key reasons for investing in international funds is global diversification
explanation: Statement (A) is false because Indian investors do have options to invest internationally through international mutual funds, feeder funds and overseas ETFs offered by Indian AMCs. Statement (B) is true because one major benefit of investing in international funds is global diversification. These funds allow Indian investors to invest in foreign markets, companies, and economies, reducing dependence on only the Indian market.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false: "Mutual fund distributors receive a unique ARN number from the Asset Management Company, which has to be renewed every three years."
options: False, since the ARN is issued by AMFI rather than the AMC
True, as mandated under SEBI guidelines
explanation: ARN (AMFI Registration Number) is issued by Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), not by individual Asset Management Companies (AMCs). Mutual fund distributors must obtain an ARN from AMFI to distribute mutual fund products in India after meeting certification and registration requirements.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the false statement(s) regarding benchmarks used for mutual fund schemes.
options: Asset Management Companies (AMCs) are permitted to select a sectoral index as the benchmark for a multi-cap mutual fund
The BSE Sensex is the most appropriate benchmark for a multi-cap fund because it includes leading large-cap companies
Both of the above are false
explanation: A sector index represents only one industry or sector, whereas a multi-cap fund invests across multiple sectors and market capitalizations. Therefore, a sector index would NOT properly reflect the fund's diversified investment universe. BSE Sensex contains only 30 large-cap companies and is therefore NOT the most appropriate benchmark for a multi-cap mutual fund, which invests across large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks. A broader index like the Nifty 500 is usually more suitable.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the correct statement relating to unclaimed dividend and redemption amounts in mutual funds.
options: The AMC may recover investment management fees within the prescribed limits
AMC can impose penalties on investors
Such unclaimed amounts are transferred to the Investor Education Fund
explanation: As per SEBI regulations, when dividend or redemption amounts remain unclaimed by investors, the AMC is allowed to deploy these unclaimed amounts in the money market instruments and earn returns on them. From these earnings, the AMC is permitted to recover investment management fees within the prescribed limits - but nothing beyond that. The unclaimed amounts are not transferred to the Investor Education Fund directly - they remain with the AMC and are kept available for the investor to claim at any time. The investor can claim the amount along with returns earned on it.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Information relating to the current economy and market outlook is generally found in which of the following mutual fund documents?
explanation: A mutual fund factsheet generally contains: current market outlook, economic commentary, portfolio strategy, sector allocation insights, recent fund performance.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: In a Conservative Hybrid Fund, what is the prescribed investment range in equity and equity-related instruments as a percentage of total assets?
explanation: A Conservative Hybrid Fund is designed for risk-averse investors who want the stability of debt with a small exposure to equity for slightly better returns. As per SEBI's categorization and rationalization circular, this fund must invest 75% to 90% in debt instruments and only 10% to 25% in equity instruments. This makes conservative hybrid funds less risky than aggressive hybrid funds.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: For mutual fund units held in a Demat account, the redemption value will be credited to which account ?
options: Through cheque payment by the stock exchange
The default bank account recorded with the mutual fund company
The account mentioned in the redemption instruction
The investor's bank account registered with the depository
explanation: When mutual fund units are held in Demat form, the redemption proceeds are credited to the bank account linked with the investor's Demat account/depository records. The depository maintains the bank details for such transactions. It is not sent by cheque nor to any random account specified in the redemption request. This rule ensures security and uniformity.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the CRISIL index best suited to be used as a benchmark for a dynamic bond fund.
explanation: A Dynamic Bond Fund invests across debt instruments with different maturities depending on interest rate movements and market conditions. Since its portfolio keeps changing dynamically, it requires a broad-based benchmark. The CRISIL Composite Bond Fund Index represents a mix of debt securities across various maturities and categories, making it suitable for comparing the performance of dynamic bond funds.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Bank-sponsored mutual funds are governed by SEBI and also by _______ .
options: Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
explanation: When a bank sponsors a mutual fund in India, it comes under the regulatory supervision of both SEBI and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). SEBI regulates the mutual fund operations, investor protection, and market-related activities, while RBI supervises the banking functions and financial stability of the sponsoring bank.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A mutual fund investor redeems 300 units at a Net Asset Value of Rs. 75 after holding the investment for 2 years. The scheme levies an exit load of 2% for redemption within one year and 1% for redemption beyond one year. Determine the redemption value that will be credited to the investor.
explanation: The investor redeems 300 units at an NAV of Rs. 75 after holding for 2 years. Since the investment was held for more than 1 year, the applicable exit load = 1%. Step 1: Calculate Gross Redemption Value Gross Value = 300 × 75 = 22,500 Step 2: Calculate Exit Load Exit Load = 1% × 22,500 =225 Step 3: Calculate Net Redemption Value Net Redemption Value = 22,500 − 225 = Rs. 22,275

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following information is generally NOT provided in a Scheme Information Document (SID) ?
options: Risk factors associated with the scheme
Complete list of securities in the portfolio
explanation: The SID (Scheme Information Document) is prepared at the time of NFO (New Fund Offer) or scheme launch. It provides details such as the investment objective, portfolio strategy/features, and risk factors of the scheme. Even after the fund is running, the portfolio keeps changing daily as the fund manager buys and sells securities. So the actual names of securities held in the portfolio are disclosed through the monthly factsheet / portfolio disclosure - not the SID.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Dividends declared on mutual fund units that are under lien will be paid to whom ?
options: The unit holder in all cases
The lien holder in all cases
Either the unit holder or the lien holder, based on the terms of issue of the mutual fund units
Either the unit holder or the lien holder, as specified in the agreement
explanation: When units are marked under a lien, it means they are pledged as security to a lender or another party. The payment of dividends on such units depends on the agreement between the unit holder and the lien holder. In some cases, dividends go to the investor, while in others they may go to the lien holder. Therefore, it depends on the terms agreed between the parties.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which is the most important factor for comparing performance of liquid funds ?
explanation: Comparing the Expense Ratio of different schemes is imperative for investors looking for the best liquid mutual fund. These schemes more or less earn similar returns. Hence, a fund with a high expense ratio will significantly reduce the returns generated. Therefore, one should invest in those liquid funds which have the lowest expense ratio.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS). A) In an ELSS - Income Distribution and Cash Withdrawal (IDCW) option -Reinvestment Plan, there would be no lock-in for the units acquired on account of IDCW B) In an ELSS - Income Distribution and Cash Withdrawal (IDCW) option -Reinvestment Plan, the units acquired on account of IDCW would have a three year lock-in from the date of allotment C) In an ELSS - Income Distribution and Cash Withdrawal (IDCW) option, no dividends can be paid due to the three year lock-in period
options: All A, B and C are true
explanation: Income Distribution and Cash Withdrawal (IDCW) plan was earlier known as the Dividend Payout Plan Equity Linked Savings Scheme is an open-ended equity linked saving scheme with a statutory lock-in of 3 years and tax benefit. The scheme has a lock-in period of three years from the date of investment. If one opts for (dividend) Income distribution cum capital withdrawal reinvestment plan, each time a dividend is reinvested, the same would also attract a 3-year lock-in. (Most AMCs have done away with this option in case of ELSS. They only allow growth option or dividend pay- out)

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The main document which authorises a company to invest in a particular Mutual Fund scheme is __________.
explanation: The Board resolution authorises the company to invest in mutual fund schemes.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the documents which have to filed with SEBI before launch of a mutual fund New Fund Offer (NFO).
options: List of benchmarks for the NFO
explanation: Units in a mutual fund scheme are offered to investors for the first time through a New Fund Offer (NFO). AMC prepares the Scheme Information Document (SID) for the NFO. This needs to be approved by the Trustees and the Board of Directors of the AMC. SID is then then filed with SEBI. (The interim changes in SID, SAI and KIM are updated through the issuance of an Addendum. Fund Factsheet contains the basic information of each scheme, the fund's performance relative to the benchmark etc. )

subject: mutual_funds
stem: KIM has to be updated ________.
explanation: As per SEBI circular in 2021 - KIM shall be updated at least once in half-year, within one month from the end of the respective half-year, based on the relevant data and information as at the end of September and March and shall be filed with SEBI.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Calculate the NAV for the following information : Value of stock 200 cr, Value of money market instruments - Rs 25 cr, Dividend accrued but not received - Rs 10 cr, Amount receivable on sale of shares - Rs 5 cr, Amount payable on purchase of shares: Rs. 10.5 cr, Fees payable - Rs 1 cr. No. of outstanding units:3 cr
explanation: NAV = (Value of stocks + Value of money market instruments + Dividend accrued but not received + Amount receivable on sale of shares - Amount payable on purchases of shares - Fees payable) / No. of outstanding units = 200 cr + 25 cr + 10 cr + 5 cr - 10.5 cr - 1 cr / 3 cr = 228.5 cr / 3 cr = 76.16

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the FALSE statement/s with respect to BENCHMARKS of mutual fund schemes. A) The right benchmark for a Sector Fund will be an index representing the respective sector B) All Equity Funds schemes will have similar benchmarks
options: Both A and B are false
Neither A nor B are false
explanation: Different type of equity funds will have different benchmarks. For eg. Some equity funds investing in large companies; while there are others that focus on mid-cap stocks or small cap stocks. S&P BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 indices are appropriate benchmarks for those equity funds that invest in large companies. For mid-cap funds, mid-cap indices such as Nifty Midcap 50 or S&P BSE Midcap are considered as better benchmarks. A sector fund would invest in only the concerned sector. Sectoral / thematic funds select sectora / thematic indices such as S&P BSE Bankex, S&P BSE FMCG Index, Nifty Infrastructure Index, Nifty Energy Index etc.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: ______ is NOT a function of AMFI.
options: Representing the mutual fund industry to the Government, RBI etc.
Undertaking studies and research of the mutual fund industry
Conducting certification exams for mutual fund distributors
explanation: AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) is the industry body that represents all mutual fund houses in India. It promotes investor education, disseminates industry data, and liaises with the government and RBI - but it does NOT conduct any certification exams. The certification exam for becoming a MF distributor is conducted by NISM (National Institute of Securities Markets) - specifically the NISM Series V-A exam.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the true statement with respect to measuring returns for Mutual Funds schemes. A. Compounded Annual Growth Rate 'CAGR' technique has been prescribed by SEBI when dividend is paid and compounding is to be considered B. CAGR is the recognized standard for calculating returns for investment horizon of greater than or equal to 1 year C. Simple Return can be calculated using the formula : (Sale Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price * 100
options: Only A and B are correct
Only A and C are correct
Only B and C are correct
All A, B and C are correct
explanation: 1. Whenever a dividend is paid - and compounding is to be considered - the CAGR technique (or the reinvestment method, as some call it) prescribed by SEBI is used 2. The return is calculated using CAGR if the holding period is over one year. If returns are less than one year, than Simple Return is calculated 3. Simple Return can be calculated with the following formula : (Sale Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price * 100

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The Valuation Policy of a mutual fund is mentioned in which document?
explanation: As per the Fair Valuation Principles laid down by SEBI : Disclosure of the valuation policy and procedures approved by the Board of the asset management company shall be made in Statement of Additional Information , on the website of the asset management company/mutual fund and at any other place where the Board may specify to ensure transparency of valuation norms to be adopted by asset management company.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement/s with respect to Addendum.
options: An Addendum must accompany the KIM
Addendum is considered to be a part of the Scheme Related Documents
Both of the above are true
None of the above are true
explanation: The addendum is considered to be a part of the scheme related documents and must accompany the KIM. Any interim changes in the Scheme Information Document (SID), Statement of Additional Information (SAI) and Key Information Memorandum (KIM) are updated through the issuance of an Addendum.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A Mutual Fund scheme gives a return of 10 % and the beta of that scheme is 0.5. The risk free return is 7.5%. What is the Treynor Ratio of this scheme ?
explanation: Treynor Ratio measures the returns earned in excess of that which would have earned on a riskless investment. Treynor Ratio Formula : (Return earned on the Scheme - Risk Free Rate) / Beta of the Scheme = (10 - 7.5) / 0.5 = 5

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the FALSE statement : 1. The investor does not have to bear a tax on the capital gains as the re-purchase of units is done by the mutual fund 2. Capital gains will be considered as Long term capital gain in case of debt funds only if the holding period is more than 3 years
explanation: Re-purchase transactions are treated as a sale of units by the investor. Therefore, there will be an element of capital gain (or capital loss) and it will be taxed accordingly. In the Finance Act of 2023, growth option of debt funds was made taxable as short term capital gains (STCG) irrespective of holding period. The Long Term capital gains tax was removed.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: __________ funds will benchmark themselves against indices based on Government securities.
explanation: Gilt funds invest only in Government securities. Therefore, indices based on Government Securities are the appropriate benchmark for Gilt funds.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify which of these statement/s is / are CORRECT.
options: When an unitholder gives a request for an Unit Certificate, it is has to be issued within 5 working days
When an unitholder gives a repurchase request, the re-purchase cheque have to be dispatched to the unitholder within 10 working days
Both of the above are correct
explanation: As per SEBI's guidelines on turnaround times for investors' transactions with the mutual fund : - Unit certificate to be issued within 5 working days of the receipt of request for the certificate. - The redemption or repurchase proceeds shall be dispatched to the unitholders within 10 working days from the date of redemption or repurchase.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the FALSE statement/s. A) During redemption, the mutual fund distributor should guide the investor to redeem those schemes which have the highest exit load B) The best strategy in selecting a mutual fund scheme for investment is that based on its past performance
options: Both A and B are false
Neither A nor B are false
explanation: Both statements A and B are false because : Past performance is only one indicator; it cannot be the sole or "best" strategy. SEBI and AMFI guidelines emphasize considering risk profile, investment objectives, fund category, and consistency - not just past returns. A distributor must act in the best interest of the investor. Suggesting redemption from the scheme with the maximum exit load would increase the investor's cost, which is against fair practice norms.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify which of these is NOT a benefit of investing in mutual funds?
explanation: Choice Overload - There are multiple mutual fund schemes offered by several mutual fund houses and multiple options within those schemes which makes it difficult for investors to choose between them.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Who has to sign the form for registering a change in the default bank account in a mutual fund folio?
options: By all the holders of the folio
By all the holders of the folio as per the mode of holding
Only by the first holder of the folio
explanation: The form for registering the change has to be signed by all the holders according to the mode of holding of the folio.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement/s. A) The Turnover Ratio will be higher in a momentum oriented investment strategy of an equity mutual fund. B) Its always simpler to invest in balanced mutual funds as compared to investing separately in equity and debt funds, but this limits choices.
options: Both A and B are true
Neither A nor B is true
explanation: Momentum mutual funds seek to capture upward trends in the market by investing in stocks that have shown strong recent performance. They follow the momentum factor, which involves buying assets that have been rising in price with the expectation that this positive trend will continue in the near future. As such funds buy and sell several times, they will have a high turnover ratio ( Turnover Ratio reflects the percentage of portfolio holdings that were changed/bought/sold/turned over in? a year) Investing in a hybrid/balanced scheme makes things simpler for the investor, because fewer scheme selection decisions need to be taken. However, the investor cannot decide the composition of portfolio and would need to go by the debt- equity mix in the investment portfolio of the schemes.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the CORRECT statement/s. A. Valuation gains are ignored. But valuation losses need to be adjusted against the profits while calculating distributable surplus. B. The Mark-to-market gains form a part of the distributable reserves in case of mutual fund Income Distribution Cum Capital Withdrawal plan
options: Both A and B are correct
Both A and B are incorrect
explanation: SEBI guidelines stipulate dividends can be paid out of distributable reserves. Mark-to-market gains are on paper - they are not realised. They will be realized when those investments are sold. So these cannot be included in distributable reserves Also Valuation gains are ignored. But valuation losses need to be adjusted against the profits. This conservative approach to calculating distributable reserves ensures that dividend is paid out of real and realized profits, after providing for all possible losses.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Risk Profilers are used to ascertain the risk appetite of an investor. State whether True or False?
explanation: Risk Profilers usually revolve around investors answering a few questions, based on which the risk appetite score gets generated. The risk profilers try to ascertain the risk appetite of the investor so that one does not sell mutual fund schemes that carry a higher risk than what the investor can handle.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Calculate the Average holding period if the portfolio turnover ratio is 25 percent.
explanation: Average Holding Period = 1 / Portfolio Turnover Ratio. Turnover ratio = 25% = 0.25. So, Average Holding Period = 1 / 0.25 = 4 years. This means the portfolio, on average, is held for four years before being completely churned.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: In which of the following cases can Goods and Service Tax (GST) be charged to the mutual fund scheme over and above the Total Expense Ratio of the scheme ?
options: GST applicable on AMC fees only can be charged to the scheme over and above the Total Expense Ratio
GST applicable on any fees must be within the Total Expense Ratio
GST applicable on distributor commission only can be charged to the scheme over and above the Total Expense Ratio
GST applicable on AMC fees as well as distributor commission can be charged to the scheme over and above the Total Expense Ratio
explanation: AMC(s) can charge GST, as per applicable Taxation Laws, to the schemes within the limits prescribed under SEBI (Mutual Fund) Regulations. - GST on fees paid on investment management and advisory fees shall be charged to the scheme in addition to the overall limits specified as per the Total Expense Ratio (TER) provisions. - The commission payable to the distributors of mutual funds may be subject to GST, as applicable in case of the ARN holder. Such tax cannot be charged to the scheme.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Management of investments by mutual funds is governed by ______ .
options: Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
explanation: SEBI is the primary regulator for the securities markets in India, which includes mutual funds. They set the rules and regulations that mutual funds must follow to ensure investor protection and market integrity. AMFI is a self-regulatory body that promotes ethical practices but does not govern mutual fund regulations. RBI primarily regulates banks and NBFCs, and its role in mutual funds is limited to specific aspects like foreign exchange regulations.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A Trail Commission is paid _______ .
options: as long as the investor stays invested in the mutual fund scheme
when the investor invests into the mutual fund scheme
when the investor exits the mutual fund scheme
explanation: Trail commission is calculated as a percentage of the net assets attributable to the units sold by the distributor. A mutual fund distributor is paid trail commission for as long as the investor's money is held in the fund.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mutual funds must publish their unaudited accounts once every six months _________ .
explanation: According to SEBI regulations, mutual funds must publish their unaudited half-yearly financial results: On the website of the Asset Management Company (AMC) On the AMFI website (optional but common practice) Additionally, they must issue a public notice in at least one national English daily and one regional language newspaper to inform investors that the results are available online. Thus, publishing on AMC website is mandatory. Publishing on AMFI is not mandatory but generally done.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following function can an Asset Management Company (AMC) do in-house?
explanation: The appointment of Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) is done by the AMC. However, It is not compulsory to appoint an RTA. The AMC can choose to handle this activity in-house. AMC cannot be a custodian or a broker. An independent custodian ensures that the securities are indeed held in the scheme for the benefit of investors, which is an important control aspect.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: _________ would not be an originator to a special purpose vehicle, in case of securitized asset.
explanation: A securitization transaction involves sale of receivables by the originator (a commercial bank, non-banking finance company, housing finance company, or a manufacturing/service company) to a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), typically set up in the form of a trust. Investors are issued rated Pass Through Certificates (PTCs), the proceeds of which are paid as consideration to the originator. (RBI will not be an originator) In this manner, the originator, by selling his loan receivables to an SPV, receives consideration from investors much before the maturity of the underlying loans.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The trustees of a mutual fund is appointed by the ______ .
explanation: The application to SEBI for registration of a mutual fund is made by the Sponsor(s). The Sponsors then appoints the Trustees. The operations of the mutual fund trust are governed by a Trust Deed, which is executed between the sponsors and the trustees.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The AMC or its Trustees are not liable for any loss to Foreign Investors arising from adverse changes in foreign exchange rates. - State whether True of False?
explanation: A Mutual Fund Scheme may be denominated in Indian Rupees (INR) which is different from the home currency for Foreign Portfolio Investors in the mutual fund units. The INR value of investments when translated into home currency by Foreign Portfolio Investors could be lower because of the currency movements. The AMC does not manage currency risk for Foreign Portfolio Investors and it is the sole responsibility of the Foreign Portfolio Investors to manage or reduce currency risk on their own. The Sponsor/Fund/Trustees/ AMC are not liable for any loss to Foreign Investors arising from such changes in exchange rates.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which information has to be included in the mutual fund application form when a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) subscribes for the units?
options: Countries of residence in the past one year
Details of investments made in the last one year
explanation: The information to be provided for mutual fund investments includes the name(s), nationality, identity proof and KYC compliance, signatures of all the holder(s), address and communication details of the first holder. In case of NRI investors, an overseas address must also be provided.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The minimum number of investors that a mutual fund scheme should have :
explanation: Every mutual fund scheme/plan should have a minimum of 20 investors and no single investor shall account for more than 25 percent of the corpus of the Scheme/Plan(s).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify which of these is NOT a function of Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) ?
options: To represent to the Government, Reserve Bank of India and other bodies on all matters relating to the mutual fund Industry
To disseminate information on the mutual fund industry and to undertake studies and research directly and/or in association with other bodies.
To conduct a certification examination for Mutual Fund distributors
To undertake a nationwide investor awareness programme to promote proper understanding of the concept and working of mutual funds.
explanation: Function of AMFI includes all of the above except - Conducting a certification examination for Mutual Fund distributors. National Institute of Securities Markets ( NISM) conducts the certification examination for Mutual Fund distributors.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Can an investor redeem any amount from a Segregated Portfolio. If Yes, than what are the restrictions?
options: There is no restriction on redemptions from a Segregated Portfolio
Only 25 % of the value of current investments can be redeemed from a Segregated Portfolio
Only 50 % of the value of current investments can be redeemed from a Segregated Portfolio
An investor cannot redeem any amount from a Segregated Portfolio from the AMC
explanation: "Segregated portfolio" means a portfolio, comprising of debt or money market instrument affected by a credit event, that has been segregated in a mutual fund scheme. No redemption or subscription is allowed in the segregated portfolio. However, in order to facilitate exit to unitholders in segregated portfolio, AMC shall enable listing of units of segregated portfolio on the recognized stock exchange.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which distributor will be covered under the due diligence process of the Asset Management Company as mandated by SEBI?
options: A distributor who has presence in more than 10 locations
A distributor who has AUM of over Rs. 100 crores from non-institutional investors
A distributor who has received commission of over Rs 25 lakhs from one mutual fund
explanation: SEBI has mandated AMCs to put in place a due diligence process to regulate distributors who qualify any one of the following criteria: - Multiple point presence (More than 20 locations) - AUM raised over Rs. 100 crores across the industry in the non-institutional category butincluding high net worth individuals (HNIs) - The commission received of over Rs. 1 Crore p.a. across industry - The commission received of over Rs. 50 Lakhs from a single mutual fund

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A Closed-end fund will have a _______ .
explanation: Close-ended Schemes have an NFO Open Date and NFO Close Date. But, they do not have a Scheme Re-opening Date, because the scheme does not sell or re-purchase units. What ever sale-purchase of units takes place is between the investors on the stock exchange. Since post-NFO sale and purchase of units happen to or from counter-party in the stock exchange-and not to or from the scheme-the unit capital of the scheme remains stable or fixed (The number of units issued by a scheme multiplied by its face value (Rs. 10) is the capital of the scheme-its Unit Capital) (In an Open-End scheme, the ongoing entry and exit of investors imply that the unit capital in an open-ended fund would keep changing on a regular basis)

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the document which authorizes a company to invest in a specific mutual fund?
options: Resolution passed in the shareholders meeting
As per the Companies Act, a company can invest in any mutual fund scheme as long it is beneficial to the interest of the shareholders, without any special authorisation
As per the Companies Act, a company cannot invest in mutual funds
explanation: Since institutional investors like Companies etc. are not natural persons, authorised individuals invest on behalf of the institution. Therefore, some additional documents are essential and one of them is - Authorisation for the investing institution to invest. This is typically in the form of a Board Resolution.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these can be a benchmark for a Banking Fund?
explanation: The S&P BSE Bankex index comprises constituents of the S&P BSE 500 that are classified as members of the banks sector as defined by the BSE industry classification system.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What does a higher portfolio turnover imply?
options: It implies a long term orientation of the fund
explanation: Portfolio Turnover is the value of Purchase and Sale of Securities during a period in a mutual fund scheme. Purchase and sale of securities entails broking costs for the scheme. Frequent churning of the portfolio would add to the transaction costs.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mr. Amit want to invest in a mutual fund scheme. He has to give the request for purchase specifying the _____ .
explanation: Purchase request in a MF scheme can only be given specifying the amount the investor will be investing. The units allotted will depend on the NAV of the date of allotment. Re-purchase (Sale) request can be given in Units to be sold or Amount required.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the FALSE statement : 1. As per AMFI guidelines, the intermediary has a no right of appeal to AMFI 2. It is not the sole responsibility of the mutual fund distributors for spreading investor awareness
explanation: One of the role and function of AMFI is : To undertake a nationwide investor awareness programme to promote proper understanding of the concept and working of mutual funds. Thus, mutual fund distributors are not solely responsible for spreading investor awareness. As per the AMFI Guidelines & Norms for Intermediaries (AGNI), the intermediary has a right of appeal to AMFI.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Different investors of the similar age group should always have the same asset allocation in their investment portfolios - State whether True or False?
explanation: Different investors have different financial goals at different age levels. In fact, investors in the same age group may also have different goals. Their financial situations may also differ. At the same time, many of the financial goals may pertain to the whole families and not just an individual. In such cases, it may not be prudent to categorize investors on the basis of age alone.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The NFO price of a mutual fund scheme was Rs. 10 and its current Net Asset Value (NAV) is Rs. 8. What would happen if the transactions were to happen at NFO price?
options: The new investors as well as the existing investors in this scheme would stand to lose
The new investors as well as the existing investors in this scheme would stand to gain
The new investors stand to gain at the cost of existing investors
The new investors stand to lose at the cost of existing investors
explanation: In mutual funds, transactions always happen at the current NAV, not at the old NFO price. Let's break down your scenario: NFO price = Rs. 10 Current NAV = Rs. 8 If, hypothetically, transactions were forced to happen at the NFO price of ?10 instead of the current NAV: New investors would be buying units at Rs. 10, even though the actual value of each unit is only ?8. That means they are overpaying and immediately incurring a loss. Existing investors would benefit, because their units (worth ?8) would be sold to new investors at ?10. This artificially props up their position at the expense of newcomers. Therefore, the correct outcome is: The new investors stand to lose at the cost of existing investors.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: State whether the statement is True or False - Investment in Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal re-investment option grows faster than Growth option as the investor gets additional units.
options: Its true for all categories of mutual fund schemes
Its false for all categories of mutual fund schemes
Its true only for equity funds
It depends on whether the fund is open-end or close-end
explanation: In a Re-investment of Income Distribution cum capital withdrawal plan, the NAV declines to the extent of dividend. The resulting NAV is called ex- dividend NAV. However, the investor does not receive the dividend in his bank account; the amount is re-invested in the same scheme and additional units are allotted to the investor. The reinvestment happens at the ex-dividend NAV. The amount invested in the fund remains the same. Only the units increases and NAV decreases. Therefore the growth is same for the Growth Option and Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal Re-investment option.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these are considered as Institutional group of investors ?
explanation: NRIs, HUFs and HNIs are considered as individual investors. Companies are non-individual investors ie. Institutional investors.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of these statement/s is/are TRUE? 1. Mutual Funds offer various options like Growth, Income distribution cum capital withdrawal / Reinvestment etc. as different investors have different preferences on how profits are to be handled 2. Interval funds offer better liquidity to investors as compared to Close-Ended mutual fund
explanation: Interval funds combine features of both open-ended and close-ended schemes. They are largely close-ended but become open-ended at pre-specified intervals. The benefit for investors is that, unlike in a purely close-ended scheme, they are not completely dependent on the stock exchange to be able to buy or sell units of the interval fund. The options offered under a scheme allow investors to structure their investments in line with their liquidity preference and tax position.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The interest rate sensitivity of a bond is determined by its maturity - State whether True or False?
explanation: The interest rate sensitivity of a bond is primarily determined by its maturity (duration). Longer-maturity bonds are more sensitive to interest rate changes than shorter-maturity bonds. This happens because a bond's price moves inversely to interest rates: - When interest rates rise, bond prices fall. - When interest rates fall, bond prices rise. Bonds with a longer maturity have more future cash flows that are affected by changes in interest rates, making them more volatile.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the false statement/s. A. Investments in mutual funds can be made on a repatriable basis by NRIs B. The mutual fund will automatically pay in Dollars when the NRI redeems his investments which were made on a repatriable basis
options: Both A and B are false
explanation: For Non-resident investors, payment is made by the AMC in Rupees and not Dollars. In case the investment has been made on a repatriable basis, and the investor wishes to transfer the money abroad, the costs associated with converting the rupees into any foreign currency would be to the account of the investor. Proceeds of investments made on a repatriable basis can be credited to an NRE ( Non-Resident External) or FCNR ( Foreign Currency Non-Resident) account, as required by the investor.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement/s : 1. The Indian inheritance laws are NOT applicable to mutual fund unit holders 2. A Power of Attorney (POA) cannot make or change nominations in a mutual fund
explanation: The Indian inheritance laws are NOT applicable to mutual fund unit holders: This statement is false. Indian inheritance laws do apply to mutual fund unit holders. In the absence of a nominee, mutual fund units are passed on to the legal heirs as per inheritance laws. A Power of Attorney (POA) cannot make or change nominations in a mutual fund: This statement is true. As per regulations, a POA holder is not allowed to add, modify, or delete nominations for mutual fund investments.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: When will an Indian investor in a US Dollar based fund benefit?
explanation: If the investor invests in the US, and the US Dollar becomes stronger during the period of his investment, he benefits; if the US Dollar weakens (i.e., Rupee becomes stronger), he loses or the portfolio returns will be lower. For eg. An investor invests Rs 80,000 to buy 1000 units of a US fund when the USDINR rate was Rs 80 per Dollar. If the US Dollar becomes stronger against Indian Rupees to say Rs. 82, he will receive Rs 82,000 when he repariates the amount to India. (Assuming the funds NAV remains the same).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: ______ is/are frequently used by media and research analysts to check the performance of various schemes of a mutual fund.
explanation: One of the most popular documents from the mutual fund is the monthly Fund Factsheet. This document is extensively used by investors, fund distributors, fund rating agencies, research analysts, media and others to access information about the various schemes of the mutual fund.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is a summary of ______ .
explanation: While an investor is expected to read all the scheme related documents, circulation of the same along with the application forms is too difficult and costly, especially if the printed forms are to be distributed. In order to ensure the investor gets access to sufficient information in spite of such a constraint, a Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is mandatorily circulated along with the application form. KIM is essentially a summary of the SID and SAI (Scheme Related Documents) . It contains the key points of these documents that are essential for the investor to know to make a decision on the suitability of the investment for their needs. It is more easily and widely distributed in the market. As per SEBI regulations, every application form is to be accompanied by the KIM.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: As the complete exposure is to a single sector, Sector Funds are high on _____ .
explanation: The sector funds invest in stocks belonging to just one sector of the economy, in order to take advantages within the said sector. The examples of such funds are: Pharma fund or Banking fund etc. Sector funds are risky because of the concentration in one sector. If the sector under-performs then the scheme's returns is likely to be very poor.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to a Gilt Fund?
options: The minimum investment in G-secs (as a percentage of total assets) is 70%
The minimum investment in G-secs (as a percentage of total assets) is 75%
The minimum investment in G-secs (as a percentage of total assets) is 80%
The minimum investment in G-secs (as a percentage of total assets) is 85%
explanation: Gilt Fund is an open-ended debt scheme investing in government securities across maturity. The minimum investment in G-secs is defined to be 80 percent of total assets (across maturity).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The return from a fund is 9 %, Standard Deviation is 0.75 and the Beta is 1.4. The risk free rate of return is 7%. What is the DENOMINATOR in the calculation of the Sharpe Ratio?
explanation: In a fraction - Eg. 21 / 38 , the number above the line (21) is called the Numerator and the number below the line (the bottom number 38) is called the Denominator The formula for Sharpe Ratio is : ( Return Earned - Risk free Return ) / Standard Deviation Here the Numerator is 'Return Earned - Risk free Return' and the Denominator is 'S tandard Deviation' So the Denominator is the Standard Deviation which is given as 0.75

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) is essentially a combination of which of the following ?
options: A one-time investment followed by a one-time redemption between two mutual fund schemes
Multiple purchases followed by multiple redemptions within the same mutual fund scheme
A lump sum investment followed by periodic redemptions between two mutual fund schemes
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) and a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) occurring simultaneously between two mutual fund schemes
explanation: A Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) allows investors to move money at regular intervals from one mutual fund scheme (usually a debt or liquid fund) to another (often an equity fund). It works like a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) from the source scheme and a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) into the target scheme, happening together. Both these actions happen simultaneously and automatically, making STP essentially a SWP + SIP combo running together between two schemes.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following is mandatory for a distributor to become empaneled with an AMC?
options: More than 10 years of mutual fund distribution experience
Completion of the Know Your Distributor (KYD) process
explanation: Before empanelment with mutual funds or AMCs, mutual fund distributors must complete the Know Your Distributor (KYD) process. The KYD process involves verification of the distributor's identity, address, bank details, and AMFI Registration Number (ARN) - ensuring that only genuine and verified intermediaries are allowed to distribute mutual funds. A SEBI registration is not required for MF distributors - they operate under an ARN (AMFI Registration Number) issued by AMFI.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following best describes the concept of Asset Allocation?
options: Choosing how many mutual fund schemes an investor should hold
Determining which asset class will generate superior returns
Allocating money among various asset categories according to financial objectives, present financial condition and risk appetite
explanation: Asset Allocation is a fundamental investment strategy that involves dividing an investment portfolio across different asset classes such as equity, debt, gold, real estate, and cash equivalents. The allocation is not random - it is carefully determined based on three key personal factors: the investor's financial goals (retirement, child's education, etc.), current financial situation (income, liabilities, time horizon), and risk profile (conservative, moderate, or aggressive).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What change regarding Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) was introduced in the Union Budget 2020?
options: DDT was abolished for all categories of mutual fund schemes
The DDT rate was reduced, but the tax continued to apply
DDT was removed only for equity-oriented mutual fund schemes, while continuing for non-equity schemes
DDT was removed only for non-equity mutual fund schemes, while continuing for equity-oriented schemes
explanation: In the Union Budget 2020, the Government abolished Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) on mutual funds. Earlier, mutual fund companies paid DDT before distributing dividends to investors. After abolition, dividend income became taxable directly in the hands of investors according to their income tax slab.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following indicates that a scheme does not benefit from economies of scale?
explanation: Economies of scale mean that larger funds can spread their expenses over more assets, reducing cost per investor. Such large funds spread costs across many investors, lowering expenses. A smaller fund size does not get this benefit because expenses are spread over a lower asset base, so costs per investor stay high. This means smaller fund size prevents economies of scale.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which document contains details such as minimum investment requirements, investor service center locations, and the process for purchasing mutual fund units?
explanation: The Key Information Memorandum (KIM) contains essential details about a mutual fund scheme in a simple and summarized form. It includes information such as minimum investment amount, investor service centres, purchase procedure, and other important scheme details. The KIM helps investors quickly understand the scheme before investing.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: An application submitted for repurchase of mutual fund units is stamped with __________ . A) ARN number of the distributor B) Automatically generated location code C) Machine identifier
explanation: As per mutual fund transaction processing rules, repurchase applications are stamped with an automatically generated location code and machine identifier. These details help in proper time-stamping and tracking of transactions for NAV applicability and audit purposes. ARN of the distributor is not part of the mandatory stamping requirement on repurchase applications.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the correct statement(s) related to risk in mutual fund schemes: A) Credit Risk Funds generally carry a higher default risk compared to Corporate Bond Funds B) The NAV of gilt funds may fluctuate significantly more than liquid funds because of changes in market yields
explanation: Credit Risk Funds chase higher returns by investing in lower-rated bonds (below AA) - this means the companies issuing these bonds have a higher chance of defaulting on repayment. Corporate Bond Funds stick to high quality AA+ and above rated bonds - much safer but with slightly lower returns. So, Credit Risk Funds have a higher default risk than Corporate Bond Funds. Gilt funds invest in long-term government bonds (sometimes 10-30 year maturity). When interest rates/yields rise, the prices of these bonds fall sharply - causing significant NAV fluctuation. Liquid funds invest in instruments maturing within 91 days, so yield changes barely affect their NAV.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Investments held in a mutual fund portfolio are valued at:
explanation: Mutual fund investments are valued using their current market price. This helps calculate the correct Net Asset Value (NAV) of the scheme every day. Face value, book value, or purchase cost may not reflect the current worth of the securities. Therefore, mutual fund portfolios are valued at market value.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The interest rate sensitivity of a mutual fund scheme having a longer average maturity is generally:
explanation: Interest rate sensitivity refers to how much the price of a bond or debt fund changes when interest rates move. Mutual funds with long average maturity hold long-term bonds, which have higher duration. Duration is the key measure of sensitivity. This is because the fund is locked into current interest rates for a longer period, making it more vulnerable to rate fluctuations. When interest rates rise, the prices of these long-term bonds fall more sharply, leading to greater volatility in the fund's NAV. Conversely, if interest rates decline, such funds benefit more, as bond prices rise significantly. Hence, investors in long maturity debt funds face higher risk and reward potential compared to short maturity funds.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following statements correctly reflects SEBI guidelines regarding Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal (IDCW), formerly known as dividends, in mutual fund schemes?
options: IDCW can be paid only from dividends earned by the scheme from its investments
IDCW may be distributed only out of distributable reserves
IDCW may be distributed only if the current NAV exceeds Rs. 10
Mutual fund schemes are prohibited from distributing IDCW to unit holders
explanation: As per SEBI guidelines, mutual fund schemes can distribute IDCW only from distributable surplus/reserves available in the scheme. Which means only from realized profits and surplus available in the scheme. The fund cannot distribute more than what it has earned and realized - preventing any artificial or funded payouts. IDCW is not guaranteed and depends on the availability of distributable reserves. It is not necessary that NAV should be above Rs. 10 for paying IDCW. Also, IDCW is not restricted only to dividends received from invested companies.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the true statement(s) regarding arbitrage funds: A) Arbitrage funds are riskier compared to equity mutual funds B) Arbitrage funds aim to exploit price inefficiencies between different market segments
explanation: Statement B is true : Arbitrage funds try to earn profit from price differences of the same security in different markets, such as cash and futures markets. It works on very simple principle - "Buy Low in one market, Sell High in another market simultaneously." Statement A is false : Since every position is hedged (covered), the risk is actually very low - much lower than regular equity funds. Therefore, arbitrage funds generally have lower risk than equity funds since positions are usually hedged.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: At what stage does a nominee become entitled to have mutual fund units transferred in their name ?
options: Once the nomination is made by the unit holders
Once the nomination is registered by the mutual fund
Upon the death of the first unit holder
Upon the death of all unit holders
explanation: In a jointly held mutual fund account, if the first holder passes away, the surviving joint holders automatically continue to hold the units. The nominee's right arises only when no registered holder remains alive.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which among the following statements about real estate investments is NOT true?
options: The ticket size for investing in real estate is usually higher compared to financial investments
Real estate investments are illiquid and cannot be readily converted into cash in a few days at a clear market price
Real estate transactions generally carry lower costs than investments in financial assets
explanation: Real estate investments involve very high transaction costs - including stamp duty, registration charges, brokerage fees, legal charges, and maintenance costs. Therefore the statement - 'Real estate transactions generally carry lower costs than investments in financial assets' is false. The other two statements are true - real estate is indeed illiquid (cannot be sold quickly at a fair price within days), and the ticket size is very high (you need lakhs or crores to invest, unlike mutual funds where you can start with Rs. 500).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the NAV if the value of stocks in a Mutual Fund scheme is Rs 100 cr, Value of Bonds is Rs 10 cr, Value of Money Market Instruments is Rs 25 cr, Dividend Accrued but not received is Rs 3 cr and Fees payable is Rs 5 cr. The number of outstanding units is 75 lacs.
explanation: NAV = (Value of stocks + Value of bonds + Value of money market instruments + Dividend accrued but not received - Fees payable) / No. of outstanding units = 100 cr + 10 cr + 25 cr + 3 cr - 5 cr / 75 lacs (75 lacs = 0.75 cr) = 133 cr / 0.75 cr = 177.33

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the transactions on which Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is applicable
options: Purchase transactions of debt mutual funds
Purchase transactions of equity mutual funds
Redemption transactions of debt mutual funds
Redemption transactions of equity mutual funds
explanation: When an investor sells units of an equity fund in the stock exchange, or offers them for repurchase to the fund, he will have to incur Securities Transaction Tax (STT) i.e., STT is applicable only on redemption/switch to other schemes/sale of units of equity oriented mutual funds whether sold on stock exchange or otherwise. STT is not applicable on purchase of units of an equity scheme. It is also not applicable to transactions in debt securities or debt mutual fund schemes.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to regulation of mutual funds in India.
options: AMFI along with SEBI regulates the mutual funds in India
The two stock exchanges NSE and BSE regulate the open-end mutual fund schemes
SEBI regulates the mutual funds in India
RBI along with SEBI regulate the bank sponsored mutual funds in India
explanation: Securities markets in India are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). It regulates, among other entities, mutual funds, depositories, custodians, registrars and transfer agents (RTAs) and credit rating agencies in the country. AMFI does not regulate the Mutual Fund. The objectives of AMFI are to define and maintain high professional and ethical standards in all areas of operation of the mutual fund industry.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify which of these is not included in the 'Fundamental Attributes' of a mutual fund scheme?
options: Aggregate fees and expenses charged to the scheme
Any safety net or guarantee provided
Liquidity provisions such as listing, repurchase, redemption
explanation: Within the Scheme Information Document, there is an important section on fundamental attributes of a scheme with following parameters on terms of issue : Terms of Issue - 1. Liquidity provisions such as listing, repurchase, redemption. 2. Aggregate fees and expenses charged to the scheme. 3. Any safety net or guarantee provided. Exit Loads do not form a part of 'Fundamental Attributes' of a scheme.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Tactical Asset Allocation is the decision that comes out of calls on the likely behaviour of the market - True or False ?
explanation: Tactical Asset Allocation is the decision that comes out of calls on the likely behaviour of the market. An investor who decides to go overweight on equities because of expectations of a rise in share markets, is taking a tactical asset allocation call.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What will be the minimum investment in corporate bonds (AA and below rated) in a Credit Risk fund?
explanation: Credit Risk Fund is an open-ended debt scheme investing in below highest rated corporate bonds. The minimum investment in corporate bonds shall be 65 percent of total assets (only in AA (excludes AA+ rated corporate bonds) and below rated corporate bonds).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The Market Value of stocks of a scheme is Rs 240 crores. Dividend accrued but not received is Rs 30 crore. The Expenses payable are Rs 10 crore. The total number of outstanding units is 120 lakhs. What is the NAV of the scheme ?
explanation: Total Market Value = Rs 240 crore Add Dividend Accrued of Rs 30 crore Less Expenses Payable of Rs 10 crore Divided by Units 120 lakhs ie. 1.20 crore units 260 cr / 1.2 cr = 216.66 NAV

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The _______ is the promoter of a Mutual Fund.
explanation: Mutual funds are constituted as Trusts. The mutual fund trust is created by one or more Sponsors, who are the main persons behind the mutual fund business.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the CORRECT statement.
options: Mutual funds can only be purchased on the stock exchange platform and they cannot be sold
All mutual funds purchased on the stock exchange platform have a mandatory lock-in period
Stock exchange mutual fund trading platform has become another channel for mutual fund companies to reach out to investors
explanation: SEBI has facilitated buying and selling of the units of open-ended mutual funds through the stock exchanges. Both National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) have extended their trading platforms to help the stock exchange brokers become a channel for investors to transact in Mutual Fund units.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Once the New Fund Offer (NFO) of a Close Ended Fund has closed, a person can buy the listed units of such close ended fund ____________.
options: At prices usually higher than NAV
At prices usually lower than NAV
At prices which can be higher or lower than NAV
Units of a Close Ended Fund cannot be bought after NFO
explanation: After the NFO of a close ended fund, sale and purchase transactions happen on the stock exchange between two different investors, and that the fund is not involved in the transaction. The transaction price is likely to be different from the NAV. Depending on the demand-supply situation for the units of the scheme on the stock exchange, the transaction price could be higher or lower than the prevailing NAV.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: ________ is prohibited as per the AMFI Code of Ethics.
options: Front running in those securities in which the mutual fund is dealing
Transaction in securities through associated brokers
Distribution of mutual fund schemes through Sponsor or its associates
explanation: Front running means buying or selling of any securities ahead of transaction of the fund, with access to information regarding the transaction which is not public and which is material to making an investment decision, so as to derive unfair advantage. As per the AMFI code of ethics - Members or any of their directors, officers or employees shall not indulge in front running.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mohit is currently studying but wants to start a business after 5 years. The present cost of starting such a business is Rs. 10 lakhs. The inflation in the economy is 9%. Which formula should be used to calculate the amount which Mohit will need 5 years down the line?
explanation: The formula for calculating the Future Value of an investment made today is FV = PV * (1 + r) ^ n The PV ie. Present Value is Rs. 10 lakhs. The inflation rate (r) is 9% ie. 0.09 and time (n) is 5 years Subsituting in the formula : FV = 10,000,00 * (1+0.09)^5

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What will happen to the scheme's Net Asset Value (NAV) after the dividend is paid?
explanation: In a mutual fund, dividend is paid out of the scheme's assets. Once the dividend is distributed, that amount is deducted from the scheme's NAV. So, immediately after the dividend payout, the NAV falls by the dividend amount.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the plan which could be used in lieu of income distribution cum capital withdrawal pay-outs?
explanation: The Income distribution cum capital withdrawal (dividend) pay-out option is for investors wanting a regular income. Systematic Withdrawal Plan(SWP) is a facility which allows an investor to withdraw a fixed amount at pre-determined intervals. Therefore an Income distribution cum capital withdrawal (dividend) pay-out option is similar to SWP. The difference is that the dividend is paid only when the fund has a surplus amount and in SWP the amount is compulsarily paid. (The dividend pay-out plan is renamed as pay-out of income distribution cum capital withdrawal, dividend re-investment plan is renamed as reinvestment of income distribution cum capital withdrawal option followed by renaming of dividend transfer plan to transfer of income distribution cum capital withdrawal plan)

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Can an investor change his mutual fund distributor?
options: Yes, but a permission from AMFI and SEBI is needed for the same
Yes, but the investor has to give a written request to the fund house
Yes, but an upfront fees have to be paid to the existing distributor to cover up his loss of income
No, a change of distributor is not permitted by SEBI
explanation: Investors can choose to change their distributor or opt for direct investing. This needs to be done through a written request by the investor to the AMC. In such cases, AMCs will need to comply, without insisting on any kind of 'No Objection Certificate' from the existing distributor.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the CORRECT statement with respect to a Fund Factsheet.
options: A Fund Factsheet has to be published only at the time of a New Fund Offer (NFO)
As per SEBI regulations, a Fund Factsheet has to be published on a monthly basis by the AMCs
A Fund Factsheet is published by AMCs on a voluntary basis
All mutual fund distributors have to mandatorily read the Fund Factsheet before recommending a scheme to their investors
explanation: A Fund Factsheet is a document that provides key information about a mutual fund scheme, such as portfolio holdings, asset allocation, and recent performance. SEBI does not legally mandate AMCs to publish a factsheet. However, most AMCs voluntarily publish it (usually monthly) to keep investors informed and improve transparency.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the true statement with respect to 'Unclaimed Dividend' and redemption amounts in mutual fund schemes.
options: The Asset Management Company can charge a penalty from the investors to refund the unclaimed dividend
The Asset Management Company can recover investment management fees from the investor but within the prescribed rates
The Asset Management Company has to transfer the unclaimed amounts to investor education fund
explanation: Unclaimed dividends/redemptions are kept aside by the AMC. They can be invested and AMCs may deduct management fees (within SEBI rules). As per SEBI rules - The mutual fund has to deploy unclaimed dividend and redemption amounts in the money market and in a separate plan of Liquid scheme floated by mutual funds especially for investing the unclaimed amounts. AMC can recover investment management and advisory fees on management of these unclaimed amounts, at a maximum rate of 0.50 percent per annum and there shall be no exit loads charged on this plan.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mr. Prakash has made an one time investment in a mutual fund scheme through a distributor. He has done no other subsequent transactions. How will the trail commission payable to the distributor be calculated ?
options: The NAV as on the date of purchase X Number of units X Rate of trail commission X Number of days the investment is held / 365
The NAV as on the date of calculation of trail commission X Number of units X Rate of trail commission X Number of days the investment is held / 365
Average of all NAVs from the date of purchase to the date of calculation of trail commission X Number of units X Rate of trail commission X Number of days the investment is held / 365
Face value of unit X Number of units X Rate of trail commission X Number of days the investment is held / 365
explanation: Trail commission is calculated as a percentage of the net assets attributable to the Units sold by the distributor. The commission payable is calculated on the daily balances and paid out periodically to the distributor as per the agreement entered into with AMC. As the trail commission is calculated on net assets, distributors benefit from increase in net assets arising out of valuation gains in the market.
