Along with this he can also define exposure limits for the branches of the firm. This facility is available only to the corporate manager.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Mr. Ashish had purchased 25 PUT options on a stock X by paying a premium of Rs 20 per put (strike price of Rs 180). The stock price has closed at Rs 240 on the exercise date. In such a situation. Mr. Ashish will choose to _____ .
options: Exercise the option but should decline giving delivery of the underlying
Exercise the option as he likes the company X and its management
explanation: Mr. Ashish has bought Put options assuming that prices will fall and he will make a profit. But the price has risen and he is in a loss. So he will choose not to exercise his option. His loss will be restricted to the premium paid.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A buyer of Out-Of-the-Money (OTM) Call option is _______ .
explanation: A buyer of a Call Option, whether ITM, ATM or OTM, is bullish and payer of premium.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The relationship between the spot price and the future price is known as _____ .
explanation: Cost of Carry is the relationship between futures prices and spot prices. For equity derivatives, carrying cost is the interest paid to finance the purchase less (minus) dividend earned.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Everest Ltd. entered into a contract with Bank of Baroda under which Everest Ltd will receive interest at 7.5% p.a. and pay interest to Bank of Baroda at MIBOR on a principal of Rs. 25 crore for a period of 3 years from today. This contract is known as ______ .
explanation: A Swap is an agreement made between two parties to exchange cash flows in the future according to a prearranged formula. Swaps are, broadly speaking, series of forward contracts. Swaps help market participants manage risk associated with volatile interest rates, currency exchange rates and commodity prices.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: An investor, who is anticipating a broad stock market fall, but is not willing to sell his entire portfolio of stocks, can offset his potential losses by shorting a certain number of Index futures.
explanation: Index derivatives are useful as a tool to hedge against the market risk. An investor with a diversified equity portfolio, who wants to protect his portfolio from any temporary correction in the stock market can sell index futures for this purpose.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Ms. Mishra sold a Put option of strike Rs 500 on PQR stock for a premium of Rs 50. The lot size is 1000. On expiry day, PQR stock closed at Rs. 440. What is Ms. Mishra's net profit (+) or loss (-) ?
explanation: When one sells a put option, the view is bullish ie. price will rise. Here the price has fallen by Rs 60 (500-440). So there is a loss of Rs 60. When one sells an option, premium is received. Premium received is Rs 50. Therefore Net loss = 60 - 50 = 10 x lot sixe of 1000 = 10,000 loss.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Each forward contract can have a different delivery location, a different maturity date and a different contract size. State whether True or False?
explanation: Forward contract is a contractual agreement between two parties to buy/sell an underlying asset at a certain future date for a particular price that is pre-decided on the date of contract. Since forwards are negotiated between two parties, the terms and conditions of contracts are customized. Each contract can have a different delivery location, maturity date and contract size.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Loss incurred from speculative transactions is allowed to be set off against which of the following?
explanation: As per tax rules, a loss from speculative transactions can be adjusted only against speculative profits. It cannot be set off against non-speculative or regular business income. Such losses may be carried forward to future years, but again only for set-off against speculative gains.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of the following statements regarding impact cost is correct ?
options: Impact cost is lower for intraday transactions
Illiquid contracts have lower impact cost
Impact cost is a fee imposed by the Exchange
Wider bid-ask spreads lead to higher impact cost
explanation: Impact cost measures the cost of executing a trade compared to the ideal price (mid-price between bid and ask). Impact cost is high when liquidity is low, and one of the strongest indicators of low liquidity is a large bid-ask spread. A wider spread means traders must buy at higher prices and sell at lower prices, increasing the slippage between the ideal price and the actual execution price. Therefore, contracts with large bid-ask spreads naturally experience higher impact costs.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A trader with limited capital had a bullish outlook on a stock. The stock price went up significantly, validating his view. Which of the following positions would have generated the highest return on his invested capital?
options: Short-selling the stock in the cash market by borrowing the shares
Taking a short position in the stock futures
Taking a long position in the stock futures
Buying the stock in the cash market
explanation: Since the trader has limited capital, leverage becomes important. A long position in stock futures requires only a margin but gives exposure to the full value of the stock. When the stock price rises significantly, the profit relative to capital invested is highest in futures. Buying in the cash market needs full funds and hence gives a lower return on capital.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The debit balance in the Mark-to-Market (MTM) margin account, as on the balance sheet date, should be classified as :
options: A current asset under loans and advances
explanation: When the Mark-to-Market (MTM) margin account shows a debit balance, it means the company has paid margin but is yet to recover it. This represents money receivable, not payable. Hence, it is shown as a current asset under loans and advances in the balance sheet, not as a liability or reserve.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of the following is true with respect to FORWARD contracts?
options: May or may not result in delivery
Always carry a settlement guarantee from a clearing corporation
explanation: Forward contracts are private, OTC agreements between two parties, and the settlement method is entirely up to them. They may choose to settle by physical delivery of the underlying asset or settle in cash based on price differences. Unlike exchange-traded futures, forwards do not have a clearing corporation guarantee, so settlement terms are flexible and customizable.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: According to regulatory guidelines, which of the following correctly describes how brokers must communicate the execution or non-execution of client orders?
options: Inform the client about the execution or non-execution of the order within two hours from the time of execution.
Inform the client about the execution or non-execution of the order within one hour from the time of execution.
Inform the client about the execution or non-execution of the order by the end of the trading day.
Inform the client immediately about the execution or non-execution of the order.
explanation: Regulatory guidelines require brokers to promptly inform clients whether their orders have been executed or not. This ensures transparency, protects investors, and allows clients to take timely decisions.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: How do stock exchanges interact with buyers and sellers?
options: By directly interacting with buyers and sellers
explanation: Exchanges do not deal directly with buyers and sellers. Instead, all trades are routed through Trading Members (brokers) who are registered with the exchange. These trading members execute client orders on the exchange platform, while clearing members handle the settlement process.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The inspection of records of stock brokers, as provided under the SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 1992, is primarily carried out to _____.
options: Check compliance with the Companies Act and related rules
Confirm that authorized persons function exclusively from the broker's office
Ensure that stock brokers do not engage in any business other than stock broking
Verify that books of accounts and other records are maintained as prescribed
explanation: Under SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, 1992, inspections are carried out to check whether brokers are maintaining proper records, books of accounts, and documents as prescribed. The focus is on compliance with SEBI's requirements for transparency, accountability, and investor protection. It is not specifically about verifying office premises, Companies Act compliance, or restricting brokers from other businesses.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Delta refers to the Rate of change in the _______ .
options: Option premium for a unit change in spot price of the underlying
Option premium for a unit change in interest rate
Option premium for a unit change in volatility of the underlying
explanation: Option premiums change with changes in the factors that determine option pricing i.e., factors such as strike price, volatility, term to maturity, etc. The sensitivities most commonly tracked in the market are known collectively as "Greeks" represented by Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega and Rho The most important of the 'Greeks' is the option's "Delta". This measures the sensitivity of the option value to a given small change in the price of the underlying asset. It may also be seen as the speed with which an option moves with respect to price of the underlying asset. Delta = Change in option premium/ Unit change in price of the underlying asset.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What should be the market-wide position limit for a stock for it to be eligible for launch in the futures and options contracts in the exchange traded equity derivatives segment in India?
explanation: As per the updated SEBI eligibility criteria for stocks to be included in the Futures & Options (F&O) segment, one of the key metrics is the Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL). A stock must have a minimum MWPL of Rs. 1,500 crore (on a rolling basis using cash market data) to be considered eligible for launch in equity derivatives contracts.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Mark-to-market margins are collected _____ .
explanation: In the futures market, profits and losses are settled on day-to-day basis - called mark to market (MTM) settlement. The exchange collects these margins (MTM margins) from the loss making participants and pays to the gainers on day-to-day basis.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: For calculating the net worth of a clearing member, which of these is/are NOT considered?
explanation: The networth of the member shall be computed as follows: Capital + Free reserves Less non-allowable assets which are : - Fixed assets - Pledged securities - Member's card - Non-allowable securities (unlisted securities) - Bad deliveries - Doubtful debts and advances - Prepaid expenses - Intangible assets - 30% marketable securities

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of these is NOT included in the Indian equity derivatives market?
explanation: Although NSE and BSE allows trading in Interest rate futures but it is not a part of equity derivatives.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What does 'Near Month' futures contract mean?
options: 'Near Month' is the current month of the futures contract
'Near Month' is the next month after the current month of the futures contract
'Near Month' is the month of expiry of the futures contract
explanation: Futures contract have a maximum of 3-month trading cycle - the near month contract (which is the 1 st / Current month ) the next month contract (which is the 2nd month ) and the far month contract (which is the 3rd month ). Thus, on May 10 th , 20XX, index and stock futures contracts on the NSE are available for trading for the near month (May 20XX), the next month (June 20XX) and the far month (July 20XX).

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: State whether True or False - A trading member of a derivatives exchange can clear his trades through a Clearing member, who may or may not be a Professional clearing member.
explanation: A trading member of a derivatives exchange can indeed clear their trades through a Clearing Member, who may or may not be a Professional Clearing Member (PCM). The PCM is a specialized clearing member who clears trades on behalf of other trading members, but a regular clearing member can also perform this function.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: If a speculator purchases a naked Call Option, this means he/she has a ______ .
explanation: A naked call option purchase means the speculator is betting that the underlying asset price will rise. Buying a call option gives the right to buy at the strike price. If the market price goes up, the call option gains value. This reflects a bullish view on the underlying asset.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: __________ guarantees the performance of exchange traded contracts.
explanation: Clearing Corporation is responsible for clearing and settlement of all trades executed in the F&O Segment of the Exchange. According to the legal principle of 'novation', the Clearing Corporation becomes the central counterparty to all trades that take place on the exchange's derivatives platform. A clearing corporation guarantees contract performance (settlement of transactions).

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When an investor gives instruction to his broker to buy a certain number of contracts at or below a specific price, the order is called as _________ .
explanation: Limit order is an order to buy or sell a contract at a specified price. The user has to specify this limit price while placing the order and the order gets executed only at this specified limit price or at a better price than that.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of these options is an example of a Calendar Spread?
options: Going short on the underpriced futures contract of one month and at the same time buying the overpriced futures contract of another month
Buying stock futures contract while at the same time shorting the stock
Buying the underpriced futures contract of one month and simultaneously selling the overpriced futures contract of another month
Going short on the stock futures contract while simultaneously buying the stock
explanation: Calendar spread refers to the arbitrage between futures contracts of different expiration months. In this strategy, the arbitrageur buys and sells the futures contracts of two different months. To execute this strategy, the arbitrageur must identify which contract to buy or sell. The principal rule of arbitrage is that one must buy the underpriced contract and sell the overpriced one. Hence, the arbitrageur needs to compute the fair price of both futures contracts and compare these with the traded prices, to decide which contract is overpriced and which one is underpriced.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is the rate of STT on the sale of an index or stock futures contract?
explanation: The Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on sale of stock futures / index is 0.05% on the price at which such futures is traded.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When does the Clearing Corporation change the initial margin requirements?
options: Clearing Corporation can continuously change the initial margin requirements according to changes in market volatility
Clearing Corporation can continuously change the initial margin requirements whenever their is an increase in trading volumes
Clearing Corporation changes the initial margin requirements periodically, based on specific instructions received from SEBI
Clearing Corporation changes the initial margin requirements periodically, after each expiry date
explanation: The initial margin is dependent on price movement of the underlying asset. As high volatility assets carry more risk, the Exchange / Clearing Corporation would charge higher initial margin on them.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Complete the sentence : Shorter the time to expiry of a PUT Option, lesser will be its _______ .
explanation: Other things being equal, options tend to lose time value each day throughout their life. This is due to the fact that the uncertainty element in the price decreases. Thus shorter the time to maturity, lower will be the time value.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The risks connected with trading in derivatives have to be laid down in which document?
options: Contract Note which is sent to the client
It can be conveyed verbally to the client
explanation: The broker is required to get a Risk Disclosure Document signed by the client, at the time of client registration. This document informs clients about the kind of risks that derivatives can involve for the client. It makes the client aware and informed about the various risks associated with derivatives trading.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to Option Spreads.
options: A bullish call spread will result in an initial cash inflow for the trader
A bearish call spread will result in an initial cash inflow for the trader
A bullish put spread will result in an initial cash outflow for the trader
A bearish put spread will result in an initial cash inflow for the trader
explanation: In a bearish call spread, there is a net in-flow of premium when the spread is initiated. A bear call spread is achieved by simultaneously selling a call option and buying a call option at a higher strike price but with the same expiration date. The maximum profit to be gained using this strategy is equal to the credit received when initiating the trade. (In a bearish put spread and bullish call spread there is a net out-flow of premium when the spread is initiated. In a bullish put spread, there is a net in-flow of premium when the spread is initiated.)

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Mr X sells one ABC stock futures contract at Rs. 745. What is his profit (+) or loss (-), if he purchases the contract back at Rs. 754 ? Lot size is 1500
explanation: When you sell a stock future contract you make a profit if the share price falls or you make a loss if the price rises. In this case, ABC stock futures has risen by Rs. 9 (754 - 745). So there will be a loss. Rs. 9 x 1500 (Lot size) = Loss of Rs 13500

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: 'SCORES' is the name given to ________ .
options: Exchange's risk management and margin system
explanation: SEBI's web-based complaints redressal system is called SCORES (Sebi COmplaints REdress System). SCORES is a centralized grievance management system with tracking mechanism to know the latest updates and time taken for complaint resolution.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Why are the margins for calendar spreads in index futures low ?
options: Because calendar spreads are not traded on an Exchange
Because calendar spreads are OTT transaction
Because the market risk is low in calendar spreads
Because calendar spreads are special transactions guaranteed by RBI
explanation: A calendar spread in index futures involves taking opposite positions in the same index with different expiry dates. Since both contracts are on the same underlying index, price movements tend to offset each other, resulting in lower market (price) risk. Because of this reduced risk, exchanges prescribe lower margin requirements for calendar spreads compared to outright futures positions.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Trader A wants to sell 20 contracts of August series at Rs 4500 and Trader B wants to sell 17 contracts of September series at Rs 4550. Lot size is 50 for both these contracts. The Initial Margin is fixed at 6%. How much Initial Margin is required to be collected from both these investors (sum of initial margins of A and B) by the broker?
explanation: Payment of Initial Margin by a broker cannot be netted against two or more clients. So he will have to pay the margin for the open position of each of his clients. So margin payable for Trader A is : 20 x 4500 x 50 (Lot size) at 6% = Rs 2,70,000 Margin payable for Trader B is : 17 x 4550 x 50 (Lot size) at 6% = Rs 2,32,050 Total = Rs 5,02,050.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The money and securities which are deposited in a clients account _______ .
options: Can be attached for meeting the obligations of the broker on his proprietary account
Cannot be attached for meeting the obligations of the broker on his proprietary account
Can or cannot be attached depends on the decision of Clearing Corporation
explanation: The securities or money deposited by clients cannot be attached for meeting broker's obligation on his proprietary account. The broker has to maintain separate client bank account for segregation of client money. Also brokers should keep margins collected from clients in a separate bank account.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: In connection with the futures market, basis is ________ .
options: The current interest rate in the economy
The difference between the futures price and spot price
explanation: The difference between the spot price and the futures price is called basis. If the futures price is greater than spot price, basis for the asset is negative. Similarly, if the spot price is greater than futures price, basis for the asset is positive.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When the volatility of the underlying stock decreases, the premium of its Call option will _______ .
explanation: Higher volatility = Higher premium, Lower volatility = Lower premium (for both call and put options). Therefore, with a decrease in volatilty, the premium on the call option decreases.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Who pays the initial margin to the exchange while entering into a futures contract?
options: Only sellers pay the initial margin
No margins are payable to the exchange by buyer or seller
Both the buyer and seller pay initial margin to the exchange
explanation: The amount one needs to deposit in the margin account at the time of entering into a futures contract is known as the initial margin. In case of futures, The buyer and seller are required to pay iinitial margin as decided by exchanges for entering into futures contract. (In case of Options, the initial margin is paid only by the sellers. The option buyers have to pay the premium)

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Mr. Manoj is Nifty trader and feels that Nifty has fallen sharply in the last few days to 17500 levels and should bounce back to 17700 levels over the next week. Which option based strategy should Mr. Manoj use to back his view?
options: He should take a long position in 17500 call and short position in 17700 call
He should take a long position in 17500 put and short position in 17100 put
He should take a short position in 17500 call and short position in 17100 call
He should take a short position in 17500 call and long position in 17700 call
explanation: He should take a long position in 17500 call and short position in 17700 call This strategy is known as a Bull Call Spread, which is used when a trader expects a moderate upward movement in the underlying asset (Nifty in this case). Long 17500 Call: This benefits from Nifty rising above 17500. Short 17700 Call: This helps reduce the cost of the trade but limits the maximum profit. Payoff Structure: If Nifty stays below 17500, both options expire worthless, and the trader loses the premium paid. If Nifty rises above 17500 but stays below 17700, the trader makes a profit. If Nifty crosses 17700, the profit is capped due to the short call at 17700

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: _________ is a cost to the market participants but is not mentioned in the contract note.
explanation: Impact cost is the cost that a buyer or seller of stocks incurs while executing a transaction due to the prevailing liquidity condition on the counter. Lower the liquidity, higher will be the impact cost. The impact cost is not reflected in the contract notes.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Identify the FALSE statement with respect to Impact Cost.
options: Impact cost is also to be considered while selecting stocks to be included in the index
Impact cost is the same for the seller and the buyer of the stock
Impact cost varies as per the transaction size
Impact cost of a stock is a measure of its liquidity
explanation: Impact cost represents the cost of executing a transaction in a given stock, for a specific predefined order size, at any given point of time. It is the cost that a buyer or seller of stocks incurs while executing a transaction due to the prevailing liquidity condition on the counter. Impact cost can be different for buyers and sellers. For eg. - If there less sellers of a particular security in the market, then the impact cost will be higher for the buyers and vice versa.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: If you are a seller of put option, you expect ___________ of the underlying asset.
explanation: When you sell a put option you expect the price to rise. Even if the price remains stable, you earn the option premium. Therefore, a seller of a put options gains in both ways - stable price or increase in price of the underlying.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: In a one-month CALL option on PQR stock with a strike price of Rs. 700 is Out-of-the money. Identify which of these could be the spot price of PQR stock?
explanation: Out-of-the-money option is one with strike price worse than the spot price for the holder of option. In other words, this option would give the holder a negative cash flow if it were exercised immediately. A call option is said to be OTM, when spot price is lower than strike price. In the above question, the strike price is 700, therefore, when the spot price of 650, it will be Out-of-the-money call option.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: An investor has implemented a Short Hedge using stock futures. This is done to protect ______ .
options: The investor's existing stock holding against an anticipated price fall
Against a price rise for a planned stock purchase in the future
Against both a stock price fall and stock price rise in the future
Against a fall in the market as a whole
explanation: A short hedge using stock futures is taken to hedge the price risk of a planned future sale of a stock. For eg. You are holding Reliance Industries share of Rs 10 lacs and need this money after 3 months. You can sell the 3-month futures of Reliance Industries to protect the amount which you need. Even if the price falls, the future amount is secured by this hedge. This is call Short Hedge.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A stock is trading at Rs 100. Mr. Ashwin buys a Straddle at a strike price of 100 and pays a premium of Rs.10 for the Call option and Rs.5 for the Put option. Based on this information, identify the correct statement.
options: The break-even point for the Call Option is Rs 110
The break-even point for the Put Option is Rs 95
This straddle has two break-even points
explanation: Mr. Ashwin buys a straddle, which means he purchases both a Call and a Put option with the same strike price of Rs. 100. He pays a premium of Rs. 10 for the call and Rs. 5 for the put. The call option will break even when the stock price rises to Rs. 110 (Rs. 100 + Rs. 10), while the put option will break even when the price falls to Rs. 95 (Rs. 100 − Rs. 5). Thus, both individual options have their own break-even levels. Since a straddle profits from large movements in either direction, it effectively has two break-even points - one above and one below the strike price. Therefore, all the statements mentioned in the question are correct, making Option (4) the right answer.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The terms of the contract are decided by mutual agreement between the parties in a futures contract. State whether True or False?
explanation: In futures market, the exchange (not the parties) decides all the terms of the contract other than price. (Forwards are bilateral over-the-counter (OTC) transactions where the terms of the contract, such as price, quantity, quality, time and place are negotiated between two parties to the contract)

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which tax is applicable on the transactions done on a recognised Indian stock exchange?
explanation: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on every purchase and sale of securities that are listed on the Indian stock exchanges. STT is levied on transactions involving equity, derivatives and equity oriented mutual funds.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Mr. Surya has gone long on April Futures on ABC stock at 1200. He will make a loss if futures price move to _______ .
explanation: A long futures position will be loss making if the price falls below the purchase price. In the above question, the purchase price is Rs 1200. Therefore, when the futures price moves to Rs 1175, there will be losses.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: If the share price of ABC share increases by Rs 5 and the delta of its option is 0.5, then by how much will the option price rise ?
explanation: Delta measures the sensitivity of the option value to a given small change in the price of the underlying asset. In this case the price has moved by Rs 5 and the delta is 0.5, So Option Price will move by Rs 5 x 0.5 = Rs 2.50

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Calculate the Intrinsic Value for the following Call option : Current price of the stock - Rs. 340. Call option of strike price Rs. 300 is quoted at Rs. 56
explanation: When the Strike Price is below the Spot Price, the Call Option is 'In the Money' ie. profitable. Intrinsic Value for a such a Call Option = Spot Price - Strike Price = 340 - 300 = 40

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: For extra-ordinary dividends above 2% of the market value of the underlying security, the amount of dividend is _____ the strike price of options on the stock.
explanation: In case of declaration of "extra-ordinary" dividend by any company, the total dividend amount (special and / or ordinary) would be reduced from all the strike prices of the option contracts on that stock. The revised strike prices would be applicable from the ex-dividend date specified by the exchange.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Speculators are those who wish to _____ risks whereas hedgers are those who wish to _____ risks.
explanation: Derivatives market helps in transfer of various risks from those who are exposed to risk but have low risk appetite to participants with high risk appetite. For example, hedgers want to give away the risk where as traders/speculators are willing to take risk.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The calculation of premium of an option is a function of _______ .
options: Time left to expiry and interest rates
The current stock price and strike price
explanation: There are five fundamental parameters on which the option price depends upon: 1) Spot price of the underlying asset 2) Strike price of the option 3) Volatility of the underlying asset's price 4) Time to expiration 5) Interest rates

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of these is true for an 'In-the-money' option ?
options: 'In-the-money' option cannot be profitably exercised by the holder immediately
explanation: In-the-money (ITM) option: This option would give the option holder a positive cash flow, if it were exercised immediately. The intrinsic value of an option refers to the amount by which the option is in-themoney i.e., the amount an option buyer will realize, before adjusting for premium paid, if he exercises the option instantly. Therefore, only in-the-money options have intrinsic value whereas at-the-money and out-of-the-money options have zero intrinsic value. The intrinsic value of an option can never be negative.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between an investor's time horizon and investment risk?
options: The time horizon has no relationship with investment risk.
A longer time horizon reduces an investor's ability to take higher risks.
A longer time horizon increases an investor's ability to take higher risks.
A shorter time horizon enables an investor to take higher risks.
explanation: An investor with a longer investment time horizon has more time to recover from short-term market fluctuations. Therefore, they can generally afford to take higher investment risks in pursuit of potentially higher returns. Conversely, a shorter time horizon usually calls for a more conservative investment approach.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A seller (writer) of a naked out-of-the-money (OTM) call option is generally considered to be _________.
explanation: A seller (writer) of a naked OTM call option is generally bearish or neutral about the underlying asset. The seller receives the option premium from the buyer when the option is sold. The seller expects the underlying price to stay below the strike price at expiry. If it stays below the strike price, the call expires worthless and the seller keeps the premium as profit. However, if the price rises significantly above the strike price, the seller can face very large or theoretically unlimited losses.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is the difference between bid and ask price called?
options: Difference between put and call option premiums
Difference between futures and forward contract prices
explanation: The difference between the bid price (the price a buyer is willing to pay) and the ask price (the price a seller is willing to accept) is called the bid-ask spread. This spread represents the transaction cost or liquidity cost in the market. A narrower spread indicates a more liquid market, while a wider spread generally indicates lower liquidity.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: As per the Cost of Carry model, the value of a futures contract is determined by:
options: Futures Price = Cost of Carry only
Futures Price = Spot Price plus Cost of Carry
Futures Price = Spot Price less Cost of Carry
explanation: According to the Cost of Carry model, the futures price is equal to the spot price plus the cost of carrying the asset until the futures contract expires. The cost of carry includes expenses such as financing, storage, and insurance, adjusted for any income earned from the asset.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The total return generated by an investment in a debt instrument ______.
options: always exceeds the interest income earned
always falls below the interest income earned
always matches the interest income received
explanation: The total return on a debt security is made up of both the interest income received and any capital gain or capital loss arising from changes in the market price of the security. Therefore, the total return may be higher than, lower than or equal to the interest income, depending on price movements.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: A Treasury Bill futures contract is quoted at Rs. 92. Calculate the market value of 10 such contracts.
explanation: Calculation: Treasury Bill Futures Price = Rs. 92 per Rs. 100 face value Contract Value (Face Value) = Rs. 2,00,000 Market Value of 1 contract = 92% × 2,00,000 = Rs. 1,84,000 Market Value of 10 contracts = 1,84,000 × 10 = Rs. 18,40,000 OR Treasury bill futures are quoted as: Price = 100 − Yield (%) If the futures price is Rs 92, that implies a yield of 8%. Contract Value : Standard T-bill futures contract size in India = Rs. 2,00,000 (face value). So, 1 contract at 92 = 1,84,000 market value ( 2,00,000 × 92 / 100 = 1,84,000) For 10 Contracts 1,84,000 × 10 = Rs. 18,40,000

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A long-term capital loss arising from an investment can be adjusted against which of the following?
options: It can be adjusted only against long-term capital gains.
It cannot be adjusted against any type of capital gain.
It can be adjusted against both long-term and short-term capital gains.
It can be adjusted only against short-term capital gains.
explanation: As per the Income-tax Act, a long-term capital loss (LTCL) can be set off only against long-term capital gains (LTCG). It cannot be adjusted against short-term capital gains (STCG).

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When a call option on an index is exercised, what does the option holder receive from the option writer?
options: A cash amount equal to the excess of the spot price over the exercise price
A cash amount equal to the excess of the exercise price over the spot price
A cash amount equal to the spot price
explanation: In index options, settlement is always in cash because there is no physical delivery of the index itself. When a call option is exercised, the holder gains if the spot price of the index is higher than the strike price. The option writer pays the difference between the spot price and the exercise price, multiplied by the lot size, to the holder. This ensures that the option holder benefits from the rise in the index without needing to own the underlying stocks.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When a futures contract on a particular asset is unavailable, market participants may use futures on a closely related asset to hedge their exposure. This strategy is known as ______.
explanation: A Cross Hedge is used when a futures contract on the exact underlying asset is not available. In such cases, the market participant hedges the exposure by using a futures contract on another asset that has a close price relationship with the underlying asset. Although it may not eliminate risk completely, it helps reduce the impact of adverse price movements.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: Which of the following situations is an example of operational risk leading to financial loss?
options: A steep fall in the equity market index
An unanticipated hike in the RBI repo rate
Default in payment by a major broker
explanation: Operational risks are those arising out of failures in internal processes, people and systems or from external events. Examples include computer system failures, frauds and errors in transaction processing.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A purchaser of a call option is granted which of the following?
options: An obligation to sell the underlying asset
An obligation to buy the underlying asset
A right to sell the underlying asset
A right to buy the underlying asset
explanation: A call option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy the underlying asset at a predetermined strike price before or on the expiry date. The buyer can choose to exercise this right only if it is beneficial. If market conditions are not favorable, the buyer may simply let the option expire, limiting the loss to the premium paid.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Among January, February, and March call options on XYZ stock, all having the same strike price, which contract is likely to have the lowest premium?
options: All contracts will have identical premiums
explanation: Option premiums are influenced by the time to expiry, volatility, and interest rates. For options with the same strike price and underlying stock, the longer the time to expiry, the higher the premium, because there is more time for the option to gain value. Among January, February, and March series, January has the shortest maturity, so its premium will be the lowest. February will be higher, and March the highest, as they allow more time for favorable price movements.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate benchmark for a Government Securities (G-Sec) Fund?
explanation: A G-Sec Fund invests primarily in Government Securities. Therefore, its benchmark should also represent the performance of government bonds. The I-Sec Sovereign Bond Index (I-BEX) tracks the performance of Government of India securities and is the most appropriate benchmark. The other indices are meant for liquid funds, hybrid funds, or money market instruments and are not suitable for a G-Sec Fund.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which type of portfolio risk can be hedged using index derivatives?
explanation: Market Risk is the risk of loss caused by changes in the overall market, such as movements in stock prices, interest rates, or market sentiment. It affects almost all securities and cannot be eliminated through diversification, but it can be reduced by using index derivatives for hedging. Index derivatives are primarily used to hedge the Market Risk of a portfolio. Since the value of an index reflects the overall movement of the market, taking positions in index futures or options helps reduce losses arising from broad market fluctuations. They cannot hedge credit, operational, or professional risks, which are unrelated to market movements.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the term used for the person or entity in whose favour units are pledged?
explanation: When mutual fund units are pledged, the investor who creates the pledge is called the pledger, while the person or institution in whose favour the units are pledged is called the pledgee. The pledgee usually accepts the units as security against a loan or other obligation and has rights over the pledged units until the obligation is fulfilled.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A mutual fund application indicates the Regular Plan, but the ARN of the distributor is not provided. What will be the status of the application?
options: It will be returned to the applicant for completing the missing details.
It will be considered under the Direct Plan.
It will be accepted under the Regular Plan.
It will be rejected as an incomplete application.
explanation: If the investor selects the Regular Plan but does not mention a valid AMFI Registration Number (ARN) of the distributor in the application form, the application is processed under the Direct Plan. This is because the ARN is mandatory for routing the investment through a distributor.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is the term used for an option whose strike price is the same as the underlying asset's market price?
explanation: An option is called "At the money" (ATM) when its strike price is equal (or very close) to the current market price of the underlying asset. At this point, the option has no intrinsic value but may still have time value.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the term used to describe a mutual fund scheme's performance relative to its benchmark return?
explanation: Mutual fund scheme returns, when compared to the benchmark return, are referred to as relative return because it shows how the scheme has performed in relation to its benchmark index. If the scheme return is higher than the benchmark, it indicates outperformance; if lower, it indicates underperformance.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: An investor sells one ABC futures contract at Rs 650. The contract has a lot size of 1000 units. If the position is squared off by purchasing it back at Rs. 628, what is the resulting profit or loss?
explanation: Futures Selling Price = Rs 650 Futures Buy-back Price = Rs 628 Lot Size = 1000 Since you first sold the futures contract (short position), you profit when the price falls. Profit per share = 650 − 628 = Rs 22 Total Profit = 22 × 1000 = Rs 22,000

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of the following is the main reason futures trading carries greater risk compared to trading the underlying equity?
explanation: Futures trading is considered riskier than trading in the underlying equity because it involves high leverage. A trader can control a large contract value by paying only a small margin, which magnifies both potential profits and potential losses.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mutual fund scheme-related documents are broadly classified into which two parts?
options: Statement of Additional Information (SAI) and Scheme Information Document (SID)
Statement of Additional Information (SAI) and Fact Sheet
Key Information Memorandum (KIM) and Scheme Information Document (SID)
explanation: Mutual fund scheme-related documents are broadly divided into two parts: the Scheme Information Document (SID) and the Statement of Additional Information (SAI). The SID contains scheme-specific details such as investment objectives, risks, and fees, while the SAI contains common information about the mutual fund that applies to all its schemes. The Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is a concise summary of the SID and is not one of the two main parts.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: The assets of a mutual fund scheme are primarily built from:
options: The Asset Management Company's capital base
Money contributed by the SEBI / AMFI
explanation: A mutual fund scheme is created by collecting money from many investors and investing this pooled amount in securities according to the scheme's investment objective. The Asset Management Company (AMC) only manages these investments and does not contribute its own capital to the scheme. Similarly, the trustees supervise the scheme but do not provide the investment money. Therefore, a mutual fund scheme is essentially a pool of investor funds.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: If a market participant expects interest rates to rise, which position is the participant most likely to take in an interest rate derivative based on a benchmark interest rate?
explanation: In interest rate derivatives, the payoff depends on the movement of interest rates. If a participant believes interest rates will rise, then the price of interest rate futures will fall (since bond prices and interest rates move inversely). To profit from this expectation, the participant should take a short position in the interest rate derivative. A short position benefits when the underlying benchmark rate increases and the derivative price declines.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the incorrect statement(s) from the following: 1. When an investor wishes to redeem, the distributor should recommend redemption from the scheme with the maximum exit load. 2. Past performance is the best criterion for selecting a mutual fund scheme.
options: Both A and B are incorrect
explanation: Both statements are incorrect. At the time of redemption, a distributor should advise the investor to redeem units in a manner that minimizes the exit load and serves the investor's best interest, not from the scheme with the maximum exit load. Similarly, p ast performance alone should never be the basis for selecting a mutual fund scheme, as it does not guarantee future returns.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the correct statement from the following regarding mutual funds.
options: Ultra-short-term debt funds invest exclusively in debt instruments with the highest credit quality.
A long-established fund is always the best investment choice because it will generate higher future returns.
While evaluating mutual funds, the expense ratio carries greater importance for debt funds than for equity funds.
explanation: In debt mutual funds, the expected returns are generally lower and more predictable than in equity funds. Therefore, a higher expense ratio can reduce the investor's net return to a greater extent, making it an important factor while comparing debt schemes. A long track record does not guarantee higher future returns, and an ultra-short-term debt fund is not required to invest only in high credit quality securities.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Many market participants prefer derivatives trading over trading the underlying asset primarily because:
options: Derivatives are easier to understand and trade
Derivatives markets are less regulated than cash markets
Derivatives provide the advantage of leverage
It carries less risk than investing in the underlying asset
explanation: Derivatives allow traders to take a much larger market position by paying only a small margin instead of the full value of the underlying asset. This feature is called leverage and is one of the main reasons many traders prefer derivatives. While leverage can increase profits, it can also increase losses, making derivatives riskier rather than less risky. Therefore, traders often choose derivatives because they provide greater exposure with a smaller initial investment.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following locations is required to have a time-stamping arrangement for mutual fund transactions?
options: AMC offices designated as Points of Acceptance
Branches of banks acting as distributors
explanation: SEBI requires a time-stamping facility only at the Official Points of Acceptance (OPAs), where mutual fund applications are officially received. The time stamp determines the applicable NAV for transactions. It is not mandatory at every AMC office or at all distributor or bank branches unless they have been designated as Official Points of Acceptance.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: An 7.5% coupon-bearing Government of India (GOI) bond is trading at Rs.100. What would its approximate Yield to Maturity (YTM)?
options: Cannot be calculated from the given information
explanation: A coupon-bearing bond pays interest based on its coupon rate. If the bond price = face value (Rs 100), then the Yield to Maturity (YTM) is equal to the coupon rate. Here: Coupon rate = 7.5% Price = Rs. 100 (par value) Therefore, YTM ≈ 7.5% If the bond traded above par (e.g., Rs 102), YTM would be less than 7.5%. If the bond traded below par (e.g., Rs 98), YTM would be greater than 7.5%.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What does the Beta of a stock statistically measure?
options: The sensitivity of a stock's price movement compared with the benchmark market index
The sensitivity of a stock's price movement compared with another similar company's stock
The fluctuation or volatility of a stock's price
The returns earned from a stock investment
explanation: Beta is a statistical measure that indicates how sensitive a stock's price is to movements in the overall market index. A beta of 1 means the stock moves in line with the market, a beta greater than 1 indicates higher volatility than the market, and a beta less than 1 indicates lower volatility. Thus, beta measures systematic risk relative to the market index.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Consider the following statements regarding international mutual funds. Which statement(s) is/are false? 1. Indian investors have no opportunity to diversify their investments outside India. 2. Movements in foreign exchange rates have no impact on the NAV of international mutual fund schemes, despite the NAV being calculated in Indian Rupees.
options: Both A and B are false
explanation: Both statements are false. Indian investors can diversify internationally by investing in international mutual fund schemes that invest in overseas securities. Also, Exchange rate movements do affect the NAV of international funds because the underlying investments are denominated in foreign currencies, while the NAV is calculated in Indian Rupees. Any appreciation or depreciation in the exchange rate impacts the rupee value of the overseas investments.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: As per regulatory requirements, redemption proceeds of mutual funds must be disbursed within the period, as specified by _________.
explanation: SEBI prescribes the maximum time limit within which mutual fund redemption proceeds must be paid to investors. Mutual funds and AMCs are required to comply with these timelines, and any delay beyond the prescribed period may require payment of interest to the investor.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A financial contract or instrument whose value is derived from another asset, known as the underlying asset, is referred to as a ______.
explanation: A derivative is a financial contract whose value is derived from the price or value of another asset, known as the underlying asset. The underlying asset may be a stock, bond, commodity, currency, interest rate, or market index. Therefore, the value of the derivative changes as the value of the underlying asset changes.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following services are available on a stock exchange platform for mutual fund transactions?
options: Investing in a new mutual fund scheme
explanation: The stock exchange platform for mutual fund transactions (such as NSE MFSS or BSE StAR MF) allows investors to carry out: Fresh subscriptions - Buying units for the first time in a scheme. Additional purchases - Adding more units to an existing investment. Redemptions - Selling units back to the fund to receive redemption value.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: For an application to invest in mutual fund units by a Non-Resident Indian (NRI), where the payment is made through an NRE/FCNR account, which of the following documents is required for the application to be considered valid?
options: Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Debit Certificate
Bank statement or passbook showing the account debit
Documentary proof of taxes paid on the remitted funds
Proof of the origin of funds deposited in the NRE account
explanation: When an NRI invests in mutual fund units using funds from an NRE or FCNR account, the application must be supported by evidence that the payment has been debited from the specified account. A bank account statement or passbook showing the debit entry serves as valid proof of payment. A Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) is generally required when payment is made through foreign remittance and not when funds are directly debited from an NRE/FCNR account.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Consider the following statements about measuring returns in mutual fund schemes. Which of them is/are correct? 1) Yields reduce the overall returns earned from an investment. 2) Absolute returns are generally used to represent returns for investments held for less than one year. 3) An NAV appreciation from Rs. 20 to Rs. 60 translates into an absolute return of 200%.
explanation: Statement (2) is correct since absolute returns are generally used to represent returns for investment periods of less than one year. Statement (3) is also correct because if the NAV increases from Rs. 20 to Rs. 60, the absolute return is [(60 − 20) ÷ 20 × 100 = 200%. Statement (1) is incorrect because yield forms a part of the total return from a mutual fund investment and does not reduce or pull down investment returns.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: Which of the following statements about interest rate futures and Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) is/are true? 1. Forward Rate Agreements determine prices primarily through mutual negotiations between counterparties. 2. Interest rate futures derive their prices through open trading on a centralized exchange platform.
explanation: Both statements are true. 1. In forward rate agreements, price discovery is mainly through bilateral negotiations between counterparties. 2. In interest rate futures, price discovery happens through free interaction of buyers and sellers on a centralized trading platform (exchange).

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A possible strike by employees at Everest Ltd.'s Pune factory may disrupt production. What type of risk does this represent?
explanation: A strike by workers in a company's factory is a company-specific event that affects only that business and not the overall market. Such risks are known as Unsystematic Risks because they are unique to a particular company or industry and can be reduced through diversification. Market-wide or systematic risks, on the other hand, affect almost all companies.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A mutual fund investor redeems 3,000 units at an NAV of Rs. 40 after holding them for 2 years. The fund charges an exit load of 2% for redemptions up to 1 year and 1% thereafter. What will be the investor's redemption amount?
explanation: Units redeemed = 3000 NAV = Rs 40 Gross Redemption Value = 3000 × 40 = Rs 1,20,000 Since the redemption is after 2 years, the applicable exit load is 1%. Exit Load = 1% of Rs 1,20,000 = Rs 1200 Net Redemption Value = 1,20,000 − 1200 = Rs 1,18,800

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is the name of the risk that occurs when derivatives and the hedged security do not move in price by the same amount?
options: Risk arising from interest rate changes
explanation: Basis risk arises because the price of the derivative and the price of the asset being hedged do not always move exactly together. The difference between the spot price of the underlying asset and the derivative price is called the basis. Changes in this difference can reduce the effectiveness of the hedge, resulting in basis risk.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: On the day a trader takes a position in a futures contract, the exchange requires ________ to cover any potential losses arising from the position.
explanation: Initial margin is the amount that the exchange requires when a trader first opens a futures position. It acts as a security deposit to cover potential losses that may arise from adverse price movements. After the position is opened, gains or losses are settled daily through mark-to-market (MTM) margin, but the initial deposit required on the first day is the initial margin. This is why the exchange asks for initial margin when the position is taken.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the asset that is widely recognized as an international asset.
explanation: Gold is considered a truly international asset because it has universal acceptance and its value is recognized across countries. Unlike real estate, debt, or equity, which are linked to specific countries, markets, or issuers, gold is traded globally and serves as a store of value irrespective of national boundaries. This makes it an effective asset for international diversification.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: An increase in interest rates will generally have what effect on the premium of a put option?
options: It increases the premium of the put option.
It decreases the premium of the put option.
It causes the put option to expire automatically.
It has no impact on the premium of a put option.
explanation: When interest rates rise, the value of put options generally falls. This happens because higher rates increase the forward price of the underlying asset, making call options more attractive while reducing the present value of the strike price received in a put. In option pricing models like Black-Scholes, this effect is captured by the Greek called rho, which is negative for puts. Thus, an increase in interest rates leads to a decrease in put premiums, while call premiums tend to rise.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: Under the current regulatory framework, cash-settled Government Bond Futures are available with expiry in which of the following months?
explanation: Cash-settled Government Bond Futures are available with both serial month contracts (near months) and quarterly month contracts. This provides market participants with flexibility for short-term as well as longer-term hedging and trading.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the maximum stock count allowed in the portfolio of a Focused Fund scheme?
explanation: A Focused Fund is an equity mutual fund that invests in a concentrated portfolio of stocks. As per SEBI's scheme categorization, a Focused Fund can invest in a maximum of 30 stocks, allowing the fund manager to take high-conviction positions instead of maintaining a widely diversified portfolio.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A company investing in mutual funds is generally required to submit several documents. Which one of the following is NOT among them?
explanation: Companies investing in mutual funds are required to submit documents like PAN card copy, memorandum and articles of association, and a board resolution authorizing the investment. However, they are not required to submit their balance sheet for this purpose.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Who must approve any proposed change in the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
explanation: Any change in the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme, such as its investment objective, fees, or structure, requires the approval of the unit holders. If the required consent is not obtained, investors must be given an exit option without any exit load. Neither SEBI, AMFI, nor stock exchanges provide this approval.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: When is the Net Asset Value (NAV) of a segregated portfolio required to be disclosed?
options: Monthly along with the fund fact sheet
explanation: A segregated portfolio is a separate portfolio created within a mutual fund to isolate distressed or defaulted debt securities after a credit event. This protects the remaining investors by separating the affected assets from the healthy assets, allowing the main portfolio to continue operating normally. When a segregated portfolio is created following a credit event, the Net Asset Value (NAV) of both the main portfolio and the segregated portfolio must be disclosed on a daily basis. This ensures transparency for investors regarding the value of the affected assets.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Under SEBI regulations, which of the following conditions makes a distributor subject to the AMC's due diligence process?
options: Having a presence in over 20 locations
Receiving commission of more than Rs. 25 lakh from one mutual fund
Assets Under Management (AUM) of more than Rs. 50 crore mobilized from non-institutional investors
All of the above mentioned criteria
explanation: As per SEBI's due diligence requirements, an AMC must carry out additional due diligence for distributors who satisfy any of the specified criteria, including: - Assets Under Management (AUM) of over Rs. 50 crore from non-institutional investors. - Commission of over Rs. 25 lakh received from a single mutual fund. - Presence in more than 20 locations.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following disclosures does not provide information about where a mutual fund scheme has invested?
explanation: NAV disclosure only shows the Net Asset Value of a mutual fund scheme on a particular date. It does not provide details of the securities or assets in which the scheme has invested. In contrast, the portfolio disclosure, fund fact sheet, and scheme-wise dashboard contain information about the scheme's investment holdings, enabling investors to understand where the fund's money has been invested.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: The quotation for a Government Bond Futures contract is expressed as ______.
options: price quoted for every Rs. 100 of face value
price quoted for every Rs. 2,000 of face value
explanation: Government Bond futures are quoted as the price per Rs. 100 face value of the underlying government security, even though the contract size is based on a larger face value. This quotation method makes pricing uniform and easy to compare with the cash market. The actual contract value is then calculated using the quoted price and the contract's face value.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Among the following, which contract is generally settled bilaterally between the contracting parties?
options: Four-month forward contract for buying Swiss Francs against the Indian Rupee
One-month futures contract on Government of India bonds
explanation: A forward contract is an over-the-counter (OTC) derivative that is privately negotiated between two parties (bilateral). Such contracts (like a four month forward contract to buy Swiss Francs against the Indian rupee) are settled bilaterally, meaning the two counterparties are responsible for fulfilling the contract without the involvement of an exchange clearing corporation. In contrast, exchange-traded options and futures, such as currency options (UDS/INR), GOI bond futures and Nifty futures, are cleared and settled through the clearing corporation.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Consider the following statements about arbitrage funds. Which of the following is true?
options: Compared with equity funds, arbitrage funds involve greater risk.
Arbitrage funds seek to benefit from price differences across different markets.
explanation: Statement 2 is true. Arbitrage funds seek to earn returns by exploiting price differences (inefficiencies) between the cash and derivatives markets etc. Statement 1 is false. Arbitrage funds generally carry lower risk than equity funds because their positions are hedged. They are not exposed to the same level of market risk as diversified equity funds.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: You purchase an call option with a strike price of Rs. 500 at a premium of Rs. 50. The option contract has a lot size of 500 shares. If you later sell the option for Rs. 35, what is your net profit or loss (in Rs)?
explanation: You purchased the call option at a premium of Rs. 50 and later sold it for Rs. 35. This results in a loss of Rs. 15 per unit. With a lot size of 500 units, the total loss is Rs. 15 × 500 = Rs. 7500. Hence, the net payoff is a loss of Rs. 7500.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The holder of an American put option has the right, without any obligation, to perform which of the following actions?
options: Sell the underlying asset to the writer on or before expiry
Sell the underlying asset to the writer only on the expiry date
Buy the underlying asset from the writer on or before expiry
Buy the underlying asset from the writer only on the expiry date
explanation: An American put option gives the buyer the right but not the obligation to sell the underlying asset to the option writer at a specified strike price. Being American style, the option can be exercised anytime on or before the expiry date (unlike European options, which can only be exercised on the expiry date).

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: If the spot price of the underlying security rises while all other variables remain constant, how will the call option premium be affected?
explanation: A call option gives the right to buy the underlying asset at a fixed strike price. When the spot price of the stock rises, the likelihood of the option finishing in-the-money increases, which raises its intrinsic value and therefore its premium. Other factors like volatility and time to expiry also affect the premium, but keeping those constant, a higher spot price directly pushes the call option premium upward.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: How does TDS apply to capital gains earned from mutual fund units?
options: Capital gains from mutual funds are exempt from TDS for all investors
TDS is applicable for non resident investors on capital gains but not for resident investors
A flat TDS of 10% applies to all investors
A flat TDS of 20% applies to all investors
explanation: For resident investors, capital gains tax is payable when filing returns, but no tax is deducted at source by the mutual fund. In contrast, for NRIs, mutual funds are required to deduct TDS on capital gains at the applicable rates before making payouts. This distinction ensures compliance with tax laws and simplifies collection from non-resident investors.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following mutual fund categories is likely to provide the greatest benefits of diversification?
explanation: A Multi asset allocation fund invests in at least three different asset classes, which helps spread risk across various types of investments. This reduces the impact of poor performance in any one asset class and provides better diversification than funds focused only on bonds, large caps or a single sector. Therefore, among the given options, it offers the best diversification benefits.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: On a stock exchange, units of a close-ended fund are bought and sold between current investors and which of the following?
options: The sponsor of the mutual fund trust
explanation: After the New Fund Offer (NFO), units of a close-ended mutual fund are listed on a stock exchange. Trading takes place between buyers and sellers (unit holders/investors) on the exchange. The mutual fund itself is not the counterparty to these transactions.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Among the following, which is considered a physical asset?
options: Units issued by a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)
explanation: A physical asset is a tangible asset that has a physical existence and can be owned directly. Real estate is a physical asset because it consists of land and buildings. Shares, REIT units and bank deposits are financial assets, as they represent financial claims rather than tangible property.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: In the context of trading, what does the term Base Price refer to?
options: The reference price used for calculating the opening price range
explanation: The base price is the reference price used by the exchange to determine the permissible price range for trading at the market opening. It is not the maximum or minimum opening price, nor is it the average closing price. Instead, it serves as the benchmark from which the opening price band is calculated.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A mutual fund unit holder is not expected to perform which of the following duties?
options: Taking investment decisions for the fund
Keeping track of their investments periodically
Understanding the risks associated with their investments
Carefully reading the Scheme Information Document (offer document) before investing
explanation: Unit holders are responsible for understanding the scheme, reading the offer document carefully, being aware of the risks involved, and monitoring their investments periodically. However, they are not responsible for making investment decisions for the mutual fund. Investment decisions are taken by the fund manager, who manages the scheme according to its investment objective.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: What are the key factors that influence interest rates within an economy?
explanation: Interest rates in an economy are influenced by several factors, including inflation, the supply of money, and the demand for money. Higher inflation generally leads to higher interest rates, while the interaction between money supply and money demand also plays a key role in determining prevailing interest rates.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Identify the true statement(s) regarding mutual fund scheme documents. 1) Every Addendum issued should be accompanied by the Key Information Memorandum (KIM). 2) The Addendum is considered a component of the scheme-related documents.
explanation: An addendum is issued whenever there are interim changes to the Scheme Information Document (SID), Statement of Additional Information (SAI), or Key Information Memorandum (KIM). It becomes a part of the scheme-related documents and must always accompany the KIM so that investors receive the latest updated information. Therefore, both the given statements are correct.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: The price of a 91-day Treasury Bill futures contract is determined using ______.
options: The underlying asset's price and the cost of carry
explanation: The price of a 91-day Treasury Bill futures contract is determined using the forward pricing approach. It is derived from the underlying Treasury Bill price along with the cost of carry, which effectively reflects the forward rate. Hence, both the forward rate and the underlying price with carry cost are used in arriving at the futures price.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following accurately reflects the preference of investors in index funds?
options: Investors generally prefer index funds with low tracking error.
Investors generally prefer index funds with high tracking error.
Tracking error is not applicable to index funds.
Tracking error does not influence investors' decisions in index funds.
explanation: Tracking error measures how closely an index fund's returns match the returns of its benchmark index. A lower tracking error indicates that the fund is replicating the index more accurately, which is the primary objective of an index fund. Therefore, investors prefer index funds with a low tracking error.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is the primary purpose of implementing a short hedge using stock futures?
options: To protect current stock holdings from an anticipated price decline
To hedge against both upward and downward price movements
To lock in the purchase price of stocks to be bought later
To safeguard against a broad market downturn
explanation: A Short Hedge using stock futures involves selling futures contracts to offset potential losses in the value of stocks already owned. If the market price of the stock falls, the loss in the portfolio is compensated by gains in the short futures position. This strategy is specifically designed to protect against downside risk in existing holdings, not against price increases or general market movements.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: When applying for mutual fund units in demat form, which of the following documents is required to be submitted along with the application?
options: A copy of the Depository Participant (DP) account statement
A copy of a recent bank statement
explanation: When an investor applies for mutual fund units in dematerialised form, the application must include proof of the demat account so that the units can be credited correctly. A copy of the Depository Participant (DP) statement provides the necessary demat account details. Proof of address and a recent bank statement are not specifically required for this purpose.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Who prepares and releases the fact sheet for a mutual fund scheme?
options: Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI
explanation: Mutual fund fact sheets are published by the AMC managing the scheme, since they are responsible for providing investors with updated information about portfolio holdings, performance, expense ratio, and other key details. SEBI sets the regulatory framework, AMFI provides industry-level data and guidelines, and credit rating agencies give ratings, but the actual fact sheet for each scheme is issued by the AMC itself.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following conditions requires an investor to provide information under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA)?
options: The investor's tax residence is other than India
The investor is a resident of the USA only
The folio was earlier registered as an NRI account only
The investment is made exclusively through an overseas bank account
explanation: FATCA requires financial institutions, including mutual funds, to collect information from investors whose tax residency is outside India. This is done to comply with global tax reporting standards and to prevent tax evasion. Even if the investor is not a U.S. resident, FATCA and CRS (Common Reporting Standard) mandate disclosure whenever the investor's tax residency lies in another country. This ensures proper reporting to the relevant tax authorities.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: The delta value of an in-the-money (ITM) call option is generally:
explanation: The delta of an option measures how much the option price changes with a change in the underlying stock price. For a call option, delta is positive because the option value rises when the stock price rises. For an in-the-money (ITM) call option), the option behaves almost like the stock itself. As the stock price increases, the call option price increases nearly one-for-one. Hence, the delta is close to +1.

subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: Under the physical settlement mechanism for Government Bond Futures, what must the seller deliver?
options: Any bond available in the seller's portfolio
Any bond from the list of eligible deliverable securities
A debt instrument with the exact coupon specified in the contract
explanation: In the physical settlement of Government Bond Futures, the seller is required to deliver any one of the bonds included in the exchange's specified basket of deliverable securities. The seller cannot deliver just any bond in possession or any Government of India bond unless it is part of the eligible deliverable basket.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: How often is the Statement of Additional Information (SAI) required to be updated?
options: Within three months from the end of the financial year
explanation: The Statement of Additional Information (SAI) contains statutory information about the mutual fund and is required to be updated regularly. As per the regulatory provisions, the SAI must be updated within three months from the end of every financial year. This requirement ensures that investors always have access to the most recent statutory information about the mutual fund, covering regulatory, operational, and compliance details.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: A trader buys a put option having a strike price of Rs. 39.50 and pays a premium of Rs. 0.50. If the bond closes at Rs. 39.50 on the expiry date, what is the trader's net payoff in Rs ?
explanation: A put option gives the buyer the right to sell at the strike price. At expiry, if the bond price is equal to the strike price (Rs. 39.50), the option has no intrinsic value and expires worthless. The buyer loses only the premium (Rs 0.50) paid to purchase the option. Therefore, the net payoff is Rs. 0 − Rs. 0.50 = - Rs. 0.50.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: Why is the expense ratio considered more significant when evaluating debt mutual fund schemes than equity mutual fund schemes?
options: The risk in debt funds depends largely on the expense ratio
It helps determine the size of the mutual fund
Debt fund returns are generally lower than equity fund returns
explanation: In debt mutual funds, the expected returns are usually modest compared to equity funds. Because of this, even a small difference in the expense ratio can significantly reduce the net returns to investors. In equity funds, higher potential returns often overshadow the impact of expenses, but in debt funds, the expense ratio plays a much larger role in evaluating performance.

subject: mutual_funds
stem: A mutual fund scheme has generated a return of 12% with a standard deviation of 0.65. If the risk-free rate of return is 6%, what is the Sharpe Ratio of the scheme?
explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is calculated as: Sharpe Ratio = (Return − Risk-free Rate) / Standard Deviation = (12% − 6%) / 0.65 = 6 / 0.65 = 9.23

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: When is the delivery price fixed in a forward contract?
options: Seven days before the maturity date
One month after the contract begins
At the end of the contract period
At the time the forward contract is entered into
explanation: In a forward contract, the buyer and seller mutually agree on the delivery price when the contract is entered into. This agreed price remains fixed throughout the life of the contract, regardless of changes in the market price of the underlying asset. Settlement takes place on the future date at this pre-agreed delivery price.

subject: equity_derivatives
stem: Which of the following is a key function performed by the derivatives market?
options: Passing market risk from investors willing to take higher risk to those with lower risk tolerance
Creating arbitrage opportunities between equity and debt markets
Improving the price discovery process by reflecting intrinsic values and market expectations
Shifting speculative transactions from regulated exchanges to unregulated markets
explanation: The derivatives market helps in improving price discovery based on actual valuations and expectations.
