stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for an Aggressive Hybrid Fund?
options: Macaulay duration of the portfolio of more than 7 years
minimum 80% in equity with max unhedged short exposure of 25%
minimum 80% allocation to equity in a maximum of 30 stocks
explanation: By SEBI definition, an Aggressive Hybrid Fund requires a 65-80% in equity and 20-35% in debt.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for a Multi-Asset Allocation Fund?
options: 40-60% in equity and 40-60% in debt (no arbitrage permitted)
minimum 35% allocation each to large-cap and mid-cap stocks
investment in at least three asset classes with a minimum 10% in each
minimum 80% allocation to equity following a contrarian strategy
explanation: By SEBI definition, a Multi-Asset Allocation Fund requires investment in at least three asset classes with a minimum 10% in each.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for an Arbitrage Fund?
options: minimum 80% allocation to equity in a maximum of 30 stocks
minimum 65% in equity, seeking arbitrage opportunities
minimum 80% allocation to equity following a contrarian strategy
explanation: By SEBI definition, an Arbitrage Fund requires a minimum 65% in equity, seeking arbitrage opportunities.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: interest_rate_derivatives
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for an Equity Savings Fund?
options: Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 3 and 4 years
Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 1 and 3 years
minimum 65% in equity and minimum 10% in debt
minimum 80% allocation to equity following a value investment strategy
explanation: By SEBI definition, an Equity Savings Fund requires a minimum 65% in equity and minimum 10% in debt.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for an Equity Long-Short SIF?
options: interval fund investing across min 2 sectors, max 75% per sector, max short 25%
minimum 80% in equity with max unhedged short exposure of 25%
minimum 80% allocation to a specific sector
minimum 80% allocation to debt and PFIs
explanation: By SEBI definition, an Equity Long-Short SIF requires a minimum 80% in equity with max unhedged short exposure of 25%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for an Equity Ex-Top 100 Long-Short SIF?
options: Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 3 and 4 years
minimum 65% outside top 100 stocks with max short exposure of 25%
minimum 80% allocation to debt instruments of banks, PSUs, and PFIs
Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 3 and 6 months
explanation: By SEBI definition, an Equity Ex-Top 100 Long-Short SIF requires a minimum 65% outside top 100 stocks with max short exposure of 25%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for a Sector Rotation Long-Short SIF?
options: minimum 80% equity, max 4 sectors, max short exposure of 25%
minimum 80% allocation to a specific sector
minimum 65% allocation to equity with flexibility across market caps
explanation: By SEBI definition, a Sector Rotation Long-Short SIF requires a minimum 80% equity, max 4 sectors, max short exposure of 25%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for a Sectoral Debt Long-Short SIF?
options: minimum 65% allocation to equity with flexibility across market caps
minimum 65% in equity, seeking arbitrage opportunities
interval fund investing across min 2 sectors, max 75% per sector, max short 25%
investment in money market instruments with maturity up to 1 year
explanation: By SEBI definition, a Sectoral Debt Long-Short SIF requires an interval fund investing across min 2 sectors, max 75% per sector, max short 25%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for a Hybrid Long-Short SIF?
options: Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 3 and 4 years
minimum 35% allocation each to large-cap and mid-cap stocks
interval fund with min 25% equity, min 25% debt, max short exposure of 25%
investment in debt and money market securities with a maturity of up to 91 days
explanation: By SEBI definition, a Hybrid Long-Short SIF requires an interval fund with min 25% equity, min 25% debt, max short exposure of 25%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI categorization, what is the primary investment mandate for a Debt Long-Short SIF?
options: interval fund across durations with limited unhedged short positions via exchange-traded derivatives
interval fund with min 25% equity, min 25% debt, max short exposure of 25%
minimum 80% allocation to equity in a maximum of 30 stocks
Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 6 and 12 months
explanation: By SEBI definition, a Debt Long-Short SIF requires an interval fund across durations with limited unhedged short positions via exchange-traded derivatives.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: When the interest rate in the economy increases, the price of existing bonds...
explanation: There is an inverse relationship between interest rates and bond prices; as rates go up, existing bond prices go down.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: ___ indicates how much money can be generated per unit of mutual fund in case the scheme is liquidated.
explanation: Net Asset Value (NAV) represents the true worth and the net realizable value per unit if the scheme's holdings are liquidated.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following is an advantage of mutual funds?
options: Convenience to buy stocks and bonds directly from the mutual fund
explanation: Mutual funds pool large sums of money, achieving economies of scale that lower transaction costs and spread research expenses.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which amongst the following categories of mutual funds have a fixed maturity date?
explanation: Close-ended funds operate for a fixed period till their maturity date, after which they cease to exist and funds are returned to investors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In the sectoral and thematic funds category, an AMC can launch...
options: As many schemes as they want, without any limit
Upto a maximum of 100 such funds per AMC
As many schemes as they want, subject to the condition that overlap between two funds is less than 50%
explanation: Under SEBI categorization, AMCs can offer multiple sectoral/thematic funds provided the portfolio overlap between any two is not more than 50%.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mutual funds are constituted as 'Trusts' in India. Who are the beneficiaries of the trust?
options: The employees of the Asset Management Company
explanation: Mutual funds are established as trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, specifically for the benefit of the investors, or unitholders.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Whose job is it to track the various corporate actions like a bonus, dividend, or rights issues in companies where the mutual fund scheme has invested?
options: Auditors of the Asset Management Company
explanation: The custodian holds the assets and is responsible for tracking and collecting corporate actions like dividends and bonuses.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: AMFI is:
options: An association of the MF AMCs in India
Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO) of MF AMCs in India
Regulator for MF AMCs in India
An association of MF distributors in India
explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is the industry association of all registered Asset Management Companies.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: For valuation of debt securities for MF NAV, the approved agency is:
explanation: AMFI has appointed CRISIL Ltd. and ICRA Ltd. to provide valuation matrices for non-traded or thinly traded debt securities.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following regulates mutual funds in India?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Association of Mutual Funds in India
Board of Trustees of mutual funds
explanation: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the primary regulator governing mutual funds and the securities market in India.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mutual funds can buy and sell securities only on delivery basis (except when using permitted derivatives/short selling). State whether this statement is True or False.
explanation: As per SEBI regulations, mutual funds must generally buy and sell securities on a delivery basis, though they are permitted to engage in authorized derivative transactions and short selling.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following statements is 'True' with respect to celebrity endorsement for mutual funds?
options: SEBI has permitted celebrity endorsement at the industry level for the purpose of increasing the awareness of mutual funds
SEBI has permitted celebrity endorsements for the promotion of individual mutual fund schemes
Celebrities can endorse only ongoing mutual fund schemes
explanation: Celebrity endorsements are strictly allowed only at the industry level to increase general awareness, not to promote specific mutual fund schemes or AMCs.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Investors have the right to specify up to _ nominees for their mutual fund investment folios.
explanation: Unitholders have the right to appoint up to 10 nominees and can specify the percentage distribution among them.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: "Please read the scheme related documents carefully" - which documents does this line refer to?
options: Scheme Information Document and audited balance sheet of the Asset Management Company
Trust deed and Key Information Memorandum
Statement of Additional Information and fund fact sheet
Scheme Information Document and Statement of Additional Information
explanation: The primary scheme related documents that investors must read are the Scheme Information Document (SID) and the Statement of Additional Information (SAI).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which of the following statements is 'TRUE' with respect to the Scheme Information Document (SID) and Statement of Additional Information (SAI)?
options: These two documents are prepared in the format prescribed by Association of Mutual Funds in India as part of AMFI's Code of Conduct
These two documents are prepared in the format prescribed by Association of Mutual Funds in India as part of AMFI's Best Practices Circular
These two documents are prepared in the format prescribed by Securities and Exchange Board of India
Each Asset Management Company is free to prepare these documents in the format they desire
explanation: The SID and SAI must be strictly prepared according to the formats prescribed by SEBI.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: The NAV of scheme is disclosed on the website of ______?
explanation: The Net Asset Value (NAV) of mutual fund schemes must be declared daily on both the AMC's website and AMFI's website.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Only individuals are allowed to distribute mutual funds in India. State whether True or False.
explanation: False. Mutual funds can be distributed by individuals as well as non-individual entities like banks, NBFCs, distribution companies, and stockbrokers.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification Examination offered by ___ is required for becoming a mutual fund distributor.
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Association of Mutual Funds in India
explanation: Distributors must pass the NISM Series-V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification Examination mandated by SEBI.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: As per the fair valuation principles laid out by SEBI, it is mandatory to disclose the valuation policy in...
options: Statement of Accounts sent to investors periodically
The fair valuation principles are not to be put in public
explanation: The valuation policy and procedures approved by the AMC board must be disclosed in the Statement of Additional Information (SAI).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In case of mutual fund schemes, dividends can be paid only out of...
options: Distributable surplus generated by the scheme
explanation: SEBI guidelines stipulate that dividends (IDCW) can only be paid out of actual, realized distributable surplus/reserves, ignoring unrealized valuation gains.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What defines an "Asset Class"?
options: A grouping of investments that exhibit similar risk and return characteristics
A list of top performing funds
The total net worth of an investor
The tax bracket of a mutual fund scheme
explanation: An asset class (like equity, fixed income, or real estate) is a broad category of investments that share similar financial characteristics and behaviors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to the time management matrix referenced for financial goals, which quadrant represents "Urgent and Important" goals?
explanation: Borrowing from Stephen Covey's matrix, Quadrant I represents tasks (or financial goals) that are both Urgent and Important.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which risk refers to the possibility of an issuer failing to meet interest or principal payment obligations on a debt security?
explanation: Credit risk strictly defines the possibility that the borrower will default on their repayment commitments.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What behavioral bias involves an investor deciding their view first, and then looking only for data that supports it?
explanation: Confirmation bias causes individuals to seek out or interpret information in a way that confirms their pre-existing beliefs.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: The tendency of investors to avoid selling a losing investment due to the psychological pain of realizing a loss is known as:
explanation: Loss aversion is the psychological phenomenon where people strongly prefer avoiding losses over acquiring equivalent gains, causing them to hold onto losers too long.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In strategic asset allocation, rebalancing a portfolio mathematically forces the investor to do what?
explanation: Rebalancing restores target allocations by selling the asset that has gone up (selling high) and buying the asset that has fallen in value (buying low).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the standard rebalancing period mandated by SEBI for schemes in the event of passive breaches (excluding Overnight/Index/ETFs)?
explanation: SEBI mandates a rebalancing period of 30 business days for all schemes (other than Index, ETFs, and Overnight funds) in case of a passive deviation from the mandate.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which document outlines the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme?
explanation: The core defining features, or Fundamental Attributes, of the scheme are documented centrally in the Scheme Information Document (SID).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What percentage of the Board of Directors of a Trustee Company must be independent?
explanation: SEBI mandates that at least two-thirds of the trustees on the Board of the trustee company must be independent directors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the minimum net-worth requirement for an Asset Management Company (AMC) under current SEBI regulations?
explanation: SEBI requires an AMC to maintain a minimum net worth of Rs. 50 crore on a continuous basis.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: To change the fundamental attributes of a scheme, the AMC must provide an exit window of at least how many days to unitholders?
explanation: Unitholders must be provided an option to exit at the prevailing NAV without any exit load for a period of not less than 30 days.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: For tracking mutual fund complaints online, SEBI has created which web-based centralized system?
explanation: SEBI SCORES is the online, centralized grievance redress system for investors in the securities market.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Category 1 Execution Only Platforms (EOPs) obtain their registration from which entity?
explanation: Category 1 EOPs act as agents of AMCs and must obtain their registration directly from AMFI.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: A sponsor must have an average net annual profit of at least how much during the preceding five years to set up a mutual fund?
explanation: One of the eligibility criteria for a mutual fund sponsor is maintaining an average net annual profit of at least Rs. 10 crore across the preceding 5 years.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What does the term 'caveat emptor' signify in the context of mutual fund investments?
explanation: Caveat emptor ('let the buyer beware') indicates that investors are presumed to have read and understood the scheme documents before investing.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which section of the Scheme Information Document (SID) displays the Risk-o-meter?
explanation: The Risk-o-meter, detailing the risk to the principal invested, must be displayed prominently on the front/cover page of the SID.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which color represents the 'Very High risk' level on the SEBI mandated Risk-o-meter?
explanation: As per the updated SEBI color-coding scheme, 'Very High risk' is represented by Red (#F70D1A).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: How frequently must the portfolio of a debt mutual fund scheme be disclosed by AMCs?
options: Fortnightly basis within 5 days of every fortnight
explanation: Unlike equity funds which are disclosed monthly, debt scheme portfolios must be disclosed on a fortnightly basis within 5 days of the fortnight.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: If a mutual fund scheme invests predominantly in unrated debt instruments, what is the regulatory procedure for their valuation?
options: Valued "in-good faith" based on AMC board-approved principles
Valued solely on the fund manager's discretion without documentation
explanation: Non-traded or unrated securities must be valued "in-good faith" based on robust valuation methods approved by the AMC's Board.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Under the AMFI Code of Conduct, what happens if an intermediary is found guilty of a proven second violation?
explanation: After a warning letter for a first offense, a proven second violation by a distributor results in the permanent cancellation of their AMFI registration.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In the event of the demise of a mutual fund distributor, trail commissions paid to the nominee are restricted to what?
options: All future assets procured by the AMC
Only assets procured by the deceased distributor prior to their demise during the validity of their ARN
explanation: The nominee receives commission solely on the AUM procured by the deceased distributor while their ARN was valid; no new business is permitted under the deceased's code.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In an interval scheme, what is the minimum duration of the transaction period when the scheme becomes open-ended?
explanation: The periods when an interval scheme opens for transactions (transaction periods) must have a minimum duration of 2 working days.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: equity_derivatives
stem: In fixed income, what does 'PV01' (or PVBP) measure?
options: The premium value of a 1-month option
The present value of 1 year's worth of coupons
The change in a bond's price in currency terms for a 1 basis-point (0.01%) change in yield
The probability of default in 1 year
explanation: PV01 indicates the monetary price sensitivity to a very small change in interest rates.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which fund category requires a minimum 65% allocation to equity, alongside a minimum 10% allocation to debt and utilizes arbitrage?
explanation: The Equity Savings Fund mixes equity, debt (min 10%), and arbitrage to meet its 65% equity minimum safely.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In a 'Sector Rotation Long-Short SIF', what is the maximum number of sectors the fund can take exposure to?
explanation: The Sector Rotation Long-Short SIF is limited to a maximum of 4 sectors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In a 'Sectoral Debt Long-Short SIF', what is the maximum permitted exposure to any single sector?
explanation: The maximum exposure to any one sector is capped at 75% of NAV.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: To which category of investors does the minimum investment threshold of Rs. 10 lakhs for a SIF NOT apply?
explanation: The minimum investment threshold does not apply to accredited investors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the minimum value of proposed assets required for an Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT) coming out with an initial offer?
explanation: The value of the proposed assets of the InvIT shall not be less than Rs. 500 crores.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which category of Execution Only Platforms (EOP) obtains registration as a Stock Broker and acts as an agent of the investor?
explanation: Category 2 EOPs must obtain registration as a Stock Broker under the EOP segment.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which debt mutual fund category must maintain a Macaulay duration of the portfolio between 6 to 12 months?
explanation: The Low Duration Fund maintains a duration of 6 to 12 months.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What behavioral bias is defined as 'judging the likelihood of an event based on information most readily available or memorable'?
explanation: The Availability Heuristic relies on immediate examples that come to mind.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: For Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs), how are the risk levels depicted?
explanation: SIFs use a 5-level Risk-Band, which is reviewed monthly.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is 'Tactical Asset Allocation'?
options: Short- to medium-term adjustments of asset allocation to exploit changing market conditions
Rebalancing exactly on the 1st of every month regardless of market levels
Investing entirely based on passive indices
Shifting entirely to cash during a bear market
explanation: Tactical allocation involves taking active views to enhance returns or reduce short-term risk.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: According to SEBI regulations, how quickly must an AMC redress investor grievances?
options: Within 45 calendar days from the date of receipt
Within 30 business days from the date of receipt
Within 21 calendar days from the date of receipt
Within 15 calendar days from the date of receipt
explanation: AMCs must redress grievances promptly, but not later than 21 calendar days.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is the minimum offer size for an initial offer of a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)?
explanation: The minimum offer size for an initial offer of a REIT will not be less than Rs. 250 crore.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Since April 2020, how are dividends (IDCW) from mutual funds taxed in the hands of the investor?
options: They are added to the investor's total income and taxed at their applicable marginal tax slab rate
They are taxed at a flat rate of 10% regardless of income
The mutual fund pays a Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) instead
explanation: Dividends are now taxable in the hands of the investor at their marginal tax rate.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which hybrid fund category requires 65-80% allocation in equity and 20-35% in debt?
explanation: The Aggressive Hybrid Fund invests predominantly in equity (65-80%).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: How frequently must Asset Management Companies (AMCs) monitor the Rs. 10 lakh minimum investment compliance for SIF investors?
options: Only at the time of initial investment
explanation: AMCs must monitor the minimum investment requirement on a daily basis.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: equity_derivatives
stem: What is a 'Calendar Spread' (Horizontal Spread)?
options: Buying and selling options with different strikes and different expiries
Buying the stock and selling futures
Simultaneously buying and selling options with the same strike but different expiry dates
Buying a call and selling a put at the same strike and expiry
explanation: A calendar spread exploits differences in time decay between different expiries.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: How is the Rs. 10 lakh minimum investment requirement for SIFs calculated by the AMC?
options: Based on the investor's total bank account balance
Across all mutual fund investments globally
At the Permanent Account Number (PAN) level across all SIF strategies of the AMC
At the individual folio level for each specific SIF scheme
explanation: The Rs. 10 lakh requirement is calculated at the PAN level across all SIF strategies of the same AMC.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: In a 'Sector Rotation Long-Short SIF', what is the minimum required investment in equity and equity-related instruments?
explanation: It requires a minimum investment of 80% in equity across the selected sectors.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: A 'Flexi-Cap Fund' must invest a minimum of what percentage in equity and equity-related instruments?
explanation: A Flexi-Cap fund requires a minimum of 65% in equity and has flexibility across market caps.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What is a 'Step-Up Bond'?
options: A bond that guarantees a step-up in credit rating
A bond whose coupon rate decreases over time
A bond whose principal amount increases daily
A bond that pays a lower coupon initially, with the coupon increasing over time
explanation: A Step-Up bond features an interest rate that increases at specified intervals.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which debt fund category requires a minimum 65% allocation to corporate bonds rated AA and below?
explanation: A Credit Risk Fund must invest at least 65% in AA and below-rated corporate bonds.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Which hybrid fund category requires 75-90% allocation in debt instruments and 10-25% in equity?
explanation: The Conservative Hybrid Fund invests predominantly in debt (75-90%).

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: Among the following debt fund categories, which typically carries the highest credit risk?
explanation: Credit Risk Funds mandate at least 65% in AA and below-rated paper, carrying the highest credit risk.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What does a 'Price Return Index' (PRI) strictly measure?
options: The inflation-adjusted return of the market
Both capital appreciation and dividend payouts
The total expense ratio of the market
Only the capital appreciation (price movement) of the index constituents
explanation: PRI only captures the capital gains of the constituents, ignoring dividend/interest income.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: What minimum percentage of its assets must an Infrastructure Debt Fund (IDF) invest in infrastructure debt securities?
explanation: An IDF must invest primarily (minimum 90% of scheme assets) in infrastructure debt securities.

source: NISM V-D Exam Prep Booklet - Comprehensive Guide & MCQs.pdf
subject: mutual_funds
stem: To earn the additional 1% commission for onboarding new individual investors from B-30 cities, how long must the investor remain invested?
options: A minimum period of one year
A minimum period of three years
